Let $\mathcal C$ be a rigid monoidal category, let $a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ and $b:Y\to Y^{\vee\vee}$, and suppress the monoidal and chosen-dual comparison maps. For $s\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)$ write $\ell_Z(s)$ and $r_Z(s)$ for its left and right actions on $Z$, transported from $s\otimes1_Z$ and $1_Z\otimes s$ by the unit constraints.

1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.
   If $r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))=\ell_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))$, this becomes
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
   In particular multiplicativity holds when every unit scalar has equal left and right actions on every object. This condition holds in a braided category, and also in a $k$-linear monoidal category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$.
4. For every endomorphism $c:X\to X$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$.

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(q\ell_{Y^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_R(p))).$$

ribbon category ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) with
chosen left duals ([[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]), braiding $c$
([[def-braiding]]) and twist $\theta$, and let $X\in\mathcal C$. Write
$X_{+1}:=X$ and $X_{-1}:=X^{\vee}$. In a strict model of $\mathcal C$
([[thm-every-braided-monoidal-category-is-monoidally-equivalent-to-a-strict-braided-one]])
there is a unique strict monoidal functor

$$F_X\colon\mathcal T\longrightarrow\mathcal C$$

from the framed oriented tangle category $\mathcal T$ with

$$F_X(+)=X,\qquad F_X(-)=X^{\vee},$$

$$F_X\bigl(X^{+}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=c_{X_\varepsilon,X_{\varepsilon'}},\qquad F_X\bigl(X^{-}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=(c_{X_{\varepsilon'},X_\varepsilon})^{-1},\qquad F_X(\cup_{+1})=\operatorname{coev}_X,\qquad F_X(\cap_{+1})=\operatorname{ev}_X,\qquad F_X(\varphi^{\pm1}_{+1})=\theta_X^{\pm1},$$

where the cup and cap are the coevaluation and evaluation maps attached to the
chosen left duals and the signs are the blackboard conventions of
[[def-the-framed-oriented-tangle-category]]. The remaining elementary tangles
of $\mathcal T$, those carrying a negative sign at a cup, cap or twist, receive
the values forced by these data through the relations. Explicitly put
$j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, with $u$ as in
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Then

$$F_X(\cup_-)=(1_{X^\vee}\otimes j_X^{-1})\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee},\qquad F_X(\cap_-)=\operatorname{ev}_{X^\vee}(j_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}),\qquad F_X(\varphi_-^{\pm1})=\theta_{X^\vee}^{\pm1}.$$

These are the right coevaluation and evaluation on $X$ induced by the ribbon
structure; they need no identification $X^{\vee\vee}=X$ on objects. For a general ribbon
category the same assignment determines a strong monoidal functor, unique up to
the canonical coherence isomorphisms of the strictification. Isotopic framed
tangles are equal morphisms of $\mathcal T$, so $F_X$ is an invariant of framed
tangles. Uniqueness needs no choice.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals, twist $\theta$
([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) and Drinfeld morphism
$u_X\colon X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ of
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Put

$$j_X:=u_X\,\theta_X\ \colon\ X\longrightarrow X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Then $j$ is a natural isomorphism: it is the composite of the natural
isomorphism $u$ with the natural automorphism $\theta$ of the identity. It is
**monoidal** up to the monoidal comparison $d_{X,Y}\colon
X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\to(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$ of the double-dual
functor,

$$j_{X\otimes Y}=d_{X,Y}\circ(j_X\otimes j_Y),$$

which is precisely the statement that $u\theta$ is the pivotal comparison
induced by the ribbon structure; the identity follows from the tensor relation
$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ for
the Drinfeld morphism together with the twist axiom
$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ and
the naturality of $\theta$. Iterating the comparison identifies
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}$ with the corresponding composite of the $j_X$ and the
coherence isomorphisms of the tensor power.

closed tangle. This is a separate convention; no generator or dual pairing

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Pivotal trace additivity and tensor multiplicativity give $d_i d_j=\sum_kN_{ij}^kd_k$. Frobenius reciprocity and the change of variable in the fusion sum then give $\sum_i d_iN_{ij}^k=\sum_i d_iN_{k,j^*}^{i}=d_kd_{j^*}=d_kd_j.$ Using the balancing formula from [F1] and summing over $i$ yields $\sum_i\theta_i d_i s_{ij} =\theta_j^{-1}\sum_{i,k}d_iN_{ij}^k\theta_kd_k =\theta_j^{-1}d_jp_+.$

A simple strand $j$ encircled by a zero-framed simple loop $i$ is the scalar $s_{ij}/d_j$ on $j$ by [F5]. Hence the $\Omega$-meridian acts by $\frac1{d_j}\sum_i d_is_{ij} =\frac{(s^2)_{0j}}{d_j} =D^2\delta_{j,0},$ where $d_j\ne0$ by [F3]. Thus $D^{-2}$ times this meridian is the projector onto the unit channel. This proves the projector identity from modular inversion.

Multiply the last identity by $s_{j^*,k}$ and sum over $j$. By [F1]–[F2], $\sum_j s_{ij}s_{j^*,k} =\sum_x s_{i^*,x}s_{xk} =(s^2)_{i^*,k} =D^2\delta_{i,k}.$ Therefore $p_+\sum_j\theta_j^{-1}d_js_{j^*,k}=D^2\theta_kd_k$. Reindexing $j$ by $j^*$ and taking $k=0$ gives $p_+p_-=D^2$; since $p_+p_-=D^2\ne0$, both Gauss sums are nonzero and $\kappa^{-1}=p_-/D$.

By [F4], a $\pm1$-framed $\Omega$ unknot evaluates to $\sum_i d_i\theta_i^{\pm1}d_i=p_\pm$. For a $+1$ blow-up, the normalization changes by $D^{-1}\kappa^{-1}p_+=1$; for a $-1$ blow-up it changes by $D^{-1}\kappa p_-=p_+p_-/D^2=1$. The empty surgery diagram gives $D^{-1}$. By [F5], a zero-framed unknot colored by $\Omega$ evaluates to $\sum_i d_i^2=D^2$, so its one-component normalization is $D^{-2}D^2=1$, the $S^2\times S^1$ value.

Apply [F6] to the full coupon-bearing graph. Its finite coend identity preserves the entire band-slide morphism with every boundary factor and exterior coupon fixed, for either two surgery components or an open colored strand slid over a surgery component. It is independent of the simple-meridian computation of step 1.2. A surgery-component slide changes the linking matrix by the integral basis congruence $B\mapsto P^{\mathsf t}BP$, preserving signature even when $B$ is singular, and preserves the number of surgery components. An open graph-strand slide changes neither surgery matrix nor component count. Therefore every normalization factor is unchanged, proving the full normalized slide identities. Together with step 3.1 this proves all the stated local move identities; it imports no relative topological move-completeness theorem.

Thus $(\pi_VB)^\perp=K$ and $\pi_VB=K^\perp$; likewise $\pi_WB=K'^\perp$. A pair $(v,w)\in B$ defines an isomorphism $\phi:K^\perp/K\to K'^\perp/K'$. Changing $w$ adds precisely $K'$, and changing $v$ adds $K$; the two projections are onto and these are their kernels. Isotropy of $B$ gives $\omega_W(w,w')=\omega_V(v,v')$, so $\phi$ is symplectic.

Choose a Lagrangian $N_0$ containing $K$. This finite construction needs no transversality: extend a basis $e_i$ of $K$ to hyperbolic pairs by choosing vectors $f_j$ with $\omega(e_i,f_j)=\delta_{ij}$, possible by nondegeneracy. Replace $f_i$ by $f_i-\frac12\sum_j\omega(f_i,f_j)e_j$ to make their pairings zero. Their span is symplectic. In its symplectic orthogonal complement, repeatedly choose a nonzero vector and a vector pairing to $1$, splitting off a symplectic plane each time. Adjoining one vector from each such plane to the $e_i$ spans the required Lagrangian. The construction ends by finite dimension.

For a Lagrangian $L\subseteq V$, put $L_K=((L\cap K^\perp)+K)/K$. It is Lagrangian in $K^\perp/K$: the inverse image $P_L=(L\cap K^\perp)+K$ is isotropic, and $P_L^\perp=(L+K)\cap K^\perp=(L\cap K^\perp)+K=P_L$. The last equality follows by writing $x=l+k$ and observing that $x,k\in K^\perp$ force $l\in K^\perp$. Here $(U\cap T)^\perp=U^\perp+T^\perp$ follows from inclusion and equal dimensions by [F3]. The relation normal form in step 1.2 gives $B(L)/K'=\phi(L_K)$ and $B^t(Q)/K=\phi^{-1}(Q_{K'})$. These are equalities of the actual subspaces containing $K'$ or $K$, not an assumption that relation images are injective.

Suppose $N_0,N\subseteq V$ both contain $K$. We prove $\mu_V(L,N_0,N)=\mu_{K^\perp/K}(L_K,N_0/K,N/K)$ by identifying their complete Wall forms. The left numerator $L\cap(N_0+N)$ lies in $K^\perp$. It projects onto the right numerator: if a representative $l+k$, with $l\in L\cap K^\perp$, lies in the sum of the two reduced spaces, then $l\in N_0+N$, since that sum contains $K$. The image of $(L\cap N_0)+(L\cap N)$ is precisely the right denominator: $l+k\in N_0$ is equivalent to $l\in N_0$, and likewise for $N$. The projection kernel $L\cap K$ is already in this denominator. Hence the Wall quotient spaces are isomorphic. A decomposition $a+b+c=0$ projects to the corresponding decomposition, and $\omega(a,b')$ descends to the quotient form because both entries lie in $K^\perp$. The isomorphism is an isometry, proving equality of signatures. By step 1.1 the same reduction holds when any two arguments contain $K$.

For arbitrary $L,P$ and $N$ containing $K$, the four-Lagrangian identity gives $\mu(L,P,N)-\mu(L,P,N_0)=\mu(L,N_0,N)-\mu(P,N_0,N)$. Reduce the two right-hand terms by step 3.1 and apply that same identity in $K^\perp/K$. Thus $\mu_V(L,P,N)=\mu_{K^\perp/K}(L_K,P_K,N/K)+\eta_K(L,P)$, where $\eta_K(L,P)=\mu_V(L,P,N_0)-\mu_{K^\perp/K}(L_K,P_K,N_0/K)$. In particular the defect is independent of $N$. The auxiliary $N_0$ disappears from the differences used below.

In step 4.1 take $N=B^t(Q)$. By step 2.1 and symplectic invariance, its reduced triple transports by $\phi$ to $(B(L)/K',B(P)/K',Q_{K'})$. Since $B(L)$ and $B(P)$ both contain $K'$, step 3.1 applied in $W$ identifies this reduced signature with $\mu_W(B(L),B(P),Q)$. Therefore $\mu_V(L,P,B^t(Q))-\mu_W(B(L),B(P),Q)=\eta_K(L,P)$, independent of $Q$. Subtract the equations for $Q$ and $R$ and use the four-Lagrangian identity on $(B(L),B(P),Q,R)$ in $W$. This yields exactly the first identity in the Statement.

Relational composition obeys $(BA)(\lambda_0)=B(A(\lambda_0))$ and $(CB)^t(\lambda_3)=B^t(C^t(\lambda_3))$ by the defining existential equations. Substitute $L=A(\lambda_0)$, $P=\lambda_1$, $Q=\lambda_2$, $R=C^t(\lambda_3)$ into step 5.1. All these spaces are Lagrangian by [F2], including inverse images by applying it to transposed relations. The resulting equality is precisely $m(B,A)+m(C,BA)=m(C,B)+m(CB,A)$. Thus adding these integer corrections gives associative weights.

For an identity relation on either side, its image or inverse image is the specified middle Lagrangian, so two arguments of $\mu$ agree and the correction is zero by step 1.1. Direct sums add corrections by that same step, including the zero-dimensional empty space. For graphs of symplectic isomorphisms the correction is $\mu(f_1\lambda_0,\lambda_1,f_2^{-1}\lambda_2)$. Transporting all three arguments by $f_2$ gives $\mu(f_2f_1\lambda_0,f_2\lambda_1,\lambda_2)$ with precisely the stated sign and order. These prove the remaining conclusions.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every subset of a manifold null set is
null, and every countable union of manifold null sets is null.

Let $M$ be a positive-dimensional smooth manifold, let $\mathcal A$ be a smooth
atlas on $M$, and let $E\subseteq M$ be $\mathcal A$-null in the sense of
[[def-null-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold]]. Then $M\setminus E$ is dense in $M$.
In particular, under Countable Choice the conclusion holds for any manifold-null
set $E$.

Let $k,m,n\ge1$ and $p\in\mathbb N$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+n+p}$ be open, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^k$. Suppose $F(a,b,\lambda_0)=0$ and $D_yF(a,b,\lambda_0)$ is invertible. Then there are neighbourhoods and a unique $C^k$ map $\varphi$ solving $F(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda)=0$. More precisely, on suitable open neighbourhoods $P$ of $(a,\lambda_0)$ and $Q$ of $b$,

$$F(x,y,\lambda)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y=\varphi(x,\lambda),$$

and

$$D\varphi(x,\lambda)=-D_yF(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda)^{-1}D_{(x,\lambda)}F(x,\varphi(x,\lambda),\lambda).$$

When no parameter block is present, this is the ordinary $C^k$ implicit function theorem.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be
$C^1$, and let $a\in U$.  If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open sets
$V,W\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that
$f|_V:V\to W$ is bijective.  Its inverse $g:W\to V$ is $C^1$, and

$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$

Thus $f$ is a local diffeomorphism at $a$.

Let $m\ge 0$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^m$ be open around
$(0,0)$, and let $F:U\to\mathbb R$ be smooth with

$$F(0,0)=0,\qquad \frac{\partial F}{\partial u}(0,0)=0,\qquad \frac{\partial^2F}{\partial u^2}(0,0)\ne0.$$

Then, after shrinking $U$, there are a sign $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}$, a smooth
function $H$ of the parameter variable, and a smooth local coordinate
change $(u,y)\mapsto (u',y)$ fixing $(0,0)$ such that

$$F(u,y)=H(y)+\varepsilon (u')^2.$$

Let $F$ be smooth near $(0,0)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^m$, assume
$dF_{(0,0)}=0$, and suppose there is a smooth local coordinate system $(s,y)$
centered at $(0,0)$, obtained from $(u,y)$ by a change of variables of the
form $(u,y)\mapsto(s,y)$, together with a smooth function $H$ near
$0\in\mathbb R^m$ such that, in these coordinates,

$$\widetilde F(s,y):=F(u(s,y),y)=F(0,0)+\varepsilon s^2+H(y), \qquad \varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}.$$

Then $0$ is a critical point of $H$, the Hessian of $H$ at $0$ is the
restriction of the Hessian of $F$ at $(0,0)$ to the $y$-coordinate subspace in
the $(s,y)$ chart, and if $\operatorname{Hess}_{(0,0)}(F)$ is nondegenerate
then so is $\operatorname{Hess}_0(H)$.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $K\subseteq M$ be compact, and let $W\subseteq M$ be open with $K\subseteq W$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:M\to [0,1]$ that equals $1$ on an open neighbourhood of $K$ and satisfies $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq W$.
Under countable choice, every smooth manifold, also with boundary, admits a Riemannian metric.

The $B_1$ rows use the smooth corank-one stratum, not the singular closed determinantal variety.

The target is the product spatial 3-jet bundle over that source. The differential of the corank equation in the remaining kernel spatial direction is $c$ (terms from differentiating the kernel vector vanish because $Au=0$). The separate avoidance of $B_{1,0}$ is compatible with, and corroborates, this calculation. change $(u,y)\mapsto (u',y)$ fixing $(0,0)$ such that

$$F(u,y)=H(y)+\varepsilon (u')^2.$$

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. For each $p\in M$, let
$\gamma_p:I_p\to M$ be the maximal integral curve through $p$, and set

$$ \mathcal D:=\{(t,p)\in\mathbb R\times M:t\in I_p\}, \qquad \Phi(t,p):=\gamma_p(t). $$

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.

Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a compact interval, and let $X_t$ be a smooth
time-dependent vector field on $M$ such that

$$ \bigcup_{t\in J}\operatorname{supp}(X_t) $$

is contained in a compact subset $K\subseteq M$. Then there is a global evolution
operator $\Psi_{t,s}:M\to M$ for all $s,t\in J$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V$ be a compact
smooth $n$-manifold with boundary and let $N$ be a smooth $n$-manifold without
boundary ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Let $F:V\times I\to N$ be a smooth map such
that $F_t:=F(\cdot,t)$ is a smooth embedding for every $t\in I$
([[def-smooth-embedding]]), and suppose $F$ is constant near the ends: for some
$\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac12)$ one has $F(x,t)=F(x,0)$ for $t\le\varepsilon$ and
$F(x,t)=F(x,1)$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon$, for all $x\in V$.

Then for every open neighbourhood $W\subseteq N$ of the compact image
$F(V\times I)$ there is a smooth map $H:N\times I\to N$ such that
$H_0=\operatorname{id}_N$, every $H_t$ is a diffeomorphism of $N$
([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]),
$$H_t\circ F_0=F_t\quad\text{for every }t\in I,$$
$H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, $H_t=\operatorname{id}_N$
for $t\le\varepsilon/2$, and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.

Let $f$ be a smooth Morse function on a finite-dimensional smooth manifold
$M$, let $g$ be a smooth Riemannian metric, and set
$X=-\operatorname{grad}_g f$. At a critical point $p$ of Morse index
$\lambda(p)$, there are local $C^1$ stable and unstable embedded disks for
the flow of $X$, of dimensions $\dim M-\lambda(p)$ and $\lambda(p)$.
They are tangent at $p$ to the positive and negative Hessian subspaces,
respectively, using $g_p$ to represent the Hessian as an endomorphism.
Their flow saturations give immersed stable and unstable manifolds wherever
the requisite finite-time flow is defined. Every tangent vector to the
stable manifold along an orbit converging to $p$ gives a variational
solution decaying exponentially in forward time; every tangent vector
to the unstable manifold gives one decaying exponentially in backward time.
This applies to the actual metric gradient; no Euclidean-gradient normal
form for $g$ is assumed.
Under countable choice, every smooth manifold, also with boundary, admits a Riemannian metric.
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold with boundary admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $K\subseteq M$ be compact, and let $W\subseteq M$ be open with $K\subseteq W$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:M\to [0,1]$ that equals $1$ on an open neighbourhood of $K$ and satisfies $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq W$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Suppose the compact closed band of a smooth function on a boundaryless manifold has only finitely many critical points, all nondegenerate. There is a smooth field $X$ with $df(X)<0$ at every noncritical point of the band and $X=(2u,-2v)$ in smaller disjoint Morse charts $f=f(p)-|u|^2+|v|^2$. It can be chosen compactly supported on $M$ and hence complete.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $W$ be a compact smooth $n$-manifold with collared boundary $\partial W=\partial_0W\sqcup\partial_1W$, let $\varphi:S^{k-1}\times D^{n-k}\to\partial_1W$ be an attaching embedding of a $k$-handle and let $\psi:S^k\times D^{n-k-1}\to\partial_1(W\cup_\varphi h^k)$ be an attaching embedding of a $(k+1)$-handle attached after it, where $0\le k\le n-1$. If the attaching sphere of $h^{k+1}$ meets the belt sphere of $h^k$ transversely in exactly one point, then $W\cup_\varphi h^k\cup_\psi h^{k+1}$ is diffeomorphic to $W$ relative to $\partial_0W$. Consequently a geometrically cancelling consecutive pair may be deleted from, or added to, any handle presentation of the same manifold; the diffeomorphism may be taken to act only in a collar of the affected boundary disc and in the two handles, so the attaching data of all later handles are carried along.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. On a compact collared triad $(W;M_0,M_1)$, every adapted excellent Morse function determines a finite handle decomposition relative to $M_0$, with one handle of index $\operatorname{ind}(p)$ per critical point. Given an adapted field, the attaching sphere is the boundary of its local unstable disk transported to the lower regular level. Conversely every finite handle decomposition relative to $M_0$ is realized by an adapted excellent Morse function with one critical point per handle, of the same index, ordered by the prescribed handle order.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $(W;M_0,M_1)$ be a compact triad with adapted
$f$ and adapted field $X$ ([[def-morse-function-adapted-to-a-cobordism]]), and
let $0<a<b<1$ be regular values. The band $K=f^{-1}[a,b]$ is compact and
disjoint from $\partial W$. If $K$ contains exactly one critical point, of index
$k$, then $W^b$ is diffeomorphic to $W^a$ with one rounded
$k$-handle attached, and the attaching sphere is the flow-transported boundary
of the unstable disk. If $K$ contains finitely many critical points, all of
index $k$ at one common value, the same conclusion holds with one disjoint
$k$-handle per critical point, and the order of attachment is immaterial. The lower sublevel is respected up to homotopy of pairs, using the common pushed-in lower copy constructed in [F1], Proof 4.1; a diffeomorphism fixing the entire original lower sublevel pointwise is not asserted.

For fixed attaching and product-collar data, two compatible smooth monotone roundings of a handle attachment are diffeomorphic by an isotopy supported in that collar. The diffeomorphism is the identity outside the collar.

derivations.claim: **Exact consequences for handles; further work is distinguished.** Near the normalized birth, choose the descending field to be the negative Euclidean gradient of $a(s)+b(s)u+c_0u^3+Q(y)$ in the smaller box. For parameters close enough to the event the two critical points and the segment between them lie in this box. The line $y=0$ is invariant; its scalar equation is $\dot u=-b(s)-3c_0u^2$. For the parameter side with two roots it has exactly one local connecting trajectory between them. No additional connecting trajectory can leave the chart: choose a fixed compact annulus between two nested balls inside this model chart. At $s=0$ the gradient has no zero on the annulus, and thus its norm has a positive lower bound $m$, uniform for all sufficiently small parameters. A negative-gradient trajectory crossing the annulus from its inner to its outer boundary has Euclidean length at least the difference of the two radii and loses function value at least $m$ times that difference, since $dF/d\ell=-|\nabla F|$ along arc length. But the two critical values converge to one another at the event. For small parameters their difference is less than this fixed positive loss, so a trajectory joining them cannot cross the annulus. Inside the chart the diagonal linear $Q$ equations force every transverse coordinate to be zero on a trajectory tending to both critical points: a growing coordinate cannot tend to zero at its positive-time end and a decaying coordinate cannot tend to zero at its negative-time end. Thus the local trajectory is also the unique global trajectory. The positive and negative $Q$ directions give transverse complementary normal directions to that trajectory. Consequently its attaching sphere and belt sphere intersect geometrically once at an intermediate level, and the actual [F6] applies. This proves that this particular elementary birth inserts a geometrically cancelling adjacent-index handle pair. It does not merely infer cancellation from the two index counts. The local coordinate model gives the framing: the negative eigenspaces supply the lower handle's core disk, the positive eigenspaces supply the cocore normal coordinates, and flow transports the attaching thickening. Hence the one intersection is a **framed** handle cancellation in the sense of the existing supplier. It is supported away from the fixed boundary collars. Later handles must be transported by the supported cancellation diffeomorphism; simply deleting the pair while forgetting the terminal parametrization is not the asserted move.

**Regular-parameter intervals: a relative left-right trivialization proved by a vector field.** Suppose $s$ varies in a sufficiently short closed interval containing no exceptional event. The finitely many critical points have smooth disjoint branches $p_j(s)$ by the parameter implicit function theorem, and their distinct critical values $c_j(s)$ stay separated. Successive square completion, with $s$ a parameter, gives smooth local embeddings $\psi_{j,s}$ with $F_s(\psi_{j,s}(z))=c_j(s)+Q_j(z).$ Put $V_{j,s}=\partial_s\psi_{j,s}\circ\psi_{j,s}^{-1}$. Differentiating the last equation gives $\partial_sF_s+dF_s(V_{j,s})=c_j'(s)$ near that critical branch. Choose a smooth scalar field $Z_s(t)$ on the value interval, supported away from $0,1$ and the fixed collar value ranges, equal to $c_j'(s)$ on disjoint neighborhoods of the values $c_j(s)$. Such a field is a finite sum of disjoint bumps following those values. Near a critical point the equation $dF_s(Y_s)=Z_s(F_s)-\partial_sF_s$ is therefore solved by $Y_s=V_{j,s}$. Away from the critical branches it is solved by $Y_s=\bigl(Z_s(F_s)-\partial_sF_s\bigr)\frac{\operatorname{grad}F_s}{|\operatorname{grad}F_s|^2}.$ A partition of unity patches these solutions because the equation is linear in $Y_s$. Take $Y_s=0$ on the fixed collar: both sides vanish there. These vector fields have compact support in the interior of $W$, so their time-dependent flow $\Phi_s$ exists throughout the short parameter interval, fixes the boundary collar, and is a diffeomorphism (use the ordinary flow theorem on the extended space with field $\partial_s+Y_s$). Let $\eta_s$ be the scalar flow of $Z_s$, initially the identity. Uniqueness for the scalar ODE gives $F_s\circ\Phi_s=\eta_s\circ F_{s_0}.$ Thus regular level surfaces, handle bands, and both incoming and outgoing identifications are carried by actual collar-fixed diffeomorphisms. The scalar flow is increasing and is a translation near each critical value, since $Z_s$ is locally constant in $t$ there; hence a transported Euclidean critical-point field retains its exact Morse model. There is no appeal to “structural stability” in this argument. A finite subdivision covers any compact parameter interval without events. If an attaching embedding at one slice is $S: S^{k-1}\times D^{n-k}\to F_{s_0}^{-1}(a)$, its transported embedding is $\Phi_s\circ S$, considered in the level $F_s^{-1}(\eta_s(a))$. If its elementary outgoing identification was $d$, it becomes $\Phi_s|_{\mathrm{out}}\circ d\circ(\Phi_s|_{\mathrm{in}})^{-1}$, with the handle part transported by the same local coordinates. These formulas are necessary: writing only that the attaching sphere is isotopic loses the terminal boundary parametrization.

**Changing the descending field inside one elementary band.** This step is local to a band with at most one critical point; it does not require a global Morse–Smale theorem. The actual local stable-manifold supplier [F4] and its complete contraction proof were read. Its displayed contraction proof extends to a smooth compact parameter interval as follows. First any given standard downward gradient-like field $X$ on such a band can be written as $-\operatorname{grad}_g f$ for a smooth metric $g$. Near its critical point use the Euclidean metric from its defining chart. Off the critical point split the tangent bundle as $\mathbb RX\oplus\ker df$ and prescribe $g(X,X)=-df(X)>0$, $g(X,v)=0$ for $v\in\ker df$, and any positive metric on $\ker df$. Then $g(X,\cdot)=-df$; convex patching of such metrics preserves that linear equation and agrees with the Euclidean metric on a smaller critical chart. Use a product metric on the fixed end collars. Thus two specified fields can be joined by the negative gradients of the convex metric path $g_\tau=(1-\tau)g_0+\tau g_1$, retaining the collar condition. For completeness, smooth dependence of the unstable disks is justified rather than assumed. The linearizations are $A_\tau=-g_\tau^{-1}\operatorname{Hess} f$, smoothly parameterized, self-adjoint for $g_\tau$, and uniformly hyperbolic on the compact parameter interval. Their positive/negative spectral subbundles vary smoothly. One elementary formula is obtained by conjugating to an ordinary symmetric matrix and taking its matrix sign $A(A^2)^{-1/2}$; the positive square root of a positive definite matrix is smooth by the implicit function theorem, since the derivative $H\mapsto RH+HR$ has eigenvalues equal to positive sums of eigenvalues of $R$ and is invertible. The projectors are $(I\pm\operatorname{sign}A)/2$. A smooth family of projectors $P_\tau$ has smooth trivializations: solve $U'=[P',P]U$, which differentiating $P_\tau U_\tau-U_\tau P_0$ shows transports the ranges and kernels. Thus fixed spectral coordinates may be used on a short parameter interval. In those coordinates the supplied proof's weighted integral operator for stable paths is $\mathcal T_{\tau,a}z(t)=e^{tA_\tau}a+\int_0^t e^{(t-r)A_\tau}P_{s,\tau}R_\tau(z(r))\,dr-\int_t^\infty e^{(t-r)A_\tau}P_{u,\tau}R_\tau(z(r))\,dr.$ Choose a common spectral gap, a smaller positive decay exponent, and a uniform cutoff radius making the contraction constant strictly less than one for all nearby $\tau$. This is possible because $R_\tau(0)=DR_\tau(0)=0$ uniformly on the compact parameter interval. The operator is smooth in $(\tau,a,z)$ on the weighted path space. To check this, each spatial derivative of the cut-off $R_\tau$ is bounded; products of decaying path variations remain bounded in the same weighted norm. Parameter derivatives of the matrix exponentials add polynomial factors in $t$ or $|t-r|$, which remain integrable after reserving a smaller exponential gap. Repeated differentiation therefore gives uniformly dominated integral operators of every finite order. Its path derivative has norm below one. Differentiating the fixed-point equation and solving by the convergent Neumann series proves smooth parameter and initial-point dependence; repeated differentiation proves every higher derivative, since the highest derivative always occurs in the same invertible linear operator $I-D_z\mathcal T$. Time reversal gives the same result for unstable disks. This is the parameter version of the supplier's actual proof, with its uniform estimates and differentiability step supplied here. Intersect the smoothly varying local unstable disk with a fixed nearby regular level below its critical value. The intersection is transverse because $df(X_\tau)<0$, so it is a smooth family of framed attaching sphere sections. Its normal coordinates come from the complementary local stable directions and vary smoothly as well. Flow their sufficiently thin thickenings down to the incoming level of the elementary band. There is no intervening critical point. On the compact part outside the local critical chart the strict descending inequality has a uniform negative bound, so these trajectories reach the incoming level in uniformly bounded time. Their hitting time is smooth by the implicit function theorem, since the derivative of $f$ along the trajectory is nonzero at the hit. Consequently the full framed attaching embeddings vary by a smooth isotopy. The same flow-plus-local-handle construction gives a smooth family of outgoing identification maps. These can be extended to ambient isotopies on the compact level surface by the actual compact-source isotopy-extension supplier, or retained as the explicit smoothly varying embeddings and outgoing maps. This proves that changing fields on an elementary band introduces only isotopy of the framed attaching embedding **with the corresponding change of the outgoing identification**. Constant changes of the chosen frame at a critical point are changes of the standard handle coordinates; if a frame component is reversed, retain that handle-coordinate automorphism explicitly. It is not a new Dehn-surgery framing integer. No classification of globally broken trajectories or same-index handle slides was used.

**A critical-value crossing gives independent framed attachments.** Take a short parameter interval with just one crossing, between nondegenerate critical branches $p(s),q(s)$, and no other critical points in the chosen height band. Use parameter Morse coordinates at the two disjoint branches and choose one smooth descending field agreeing with the Euclidean models there; partition of unity constructs it exactly as in the read supplier [F5]. At the crossing parameter their values agree, say at $c$. Choose the same fixed positive model height drop $\epsilon$ at each critical point, so that each local unstable sphere section has height $F_s(p(s))-\epsilon$ or $F_s(q(s))-\epsilon$. For $s$ close enough to the crossing both sections lie strictly below **both** critical values. All flow from those sections to a lower regular level $a$ therefore takes place in a region without critical points. The corresponding unstable disks cannot hit the other critical point before reaching their sections: the function drop to each section is $\epsilon$, while the separation of the two critical values is less than $\epsilon$; choose the local disk in its own disjoint Morse chart. Thus the global attaching spheres in $F_s^{-1}(a)$ are disjoint. Equivalently, distinct points on them have backward limits at different critical points, so flow uniqueness forbids an intersection. By compactness, choose disjoint sufficiently thin framed attaching neighborhoods for both. The whole band is obtained by attaching these two disjoint framed handles and then a regular product to an upper level $b$. This follows from the same simultaneous local-handle construction and compact regular-flow comparison as the read [F7]; it does not require their indices to agree, since the charts, local function modifications, and all attaching neighborhoods are disjoint. One can also cross the two distinct critical heights in either order. Disjoint quotient attachments commute: both iterated quotients identify exactly the same two disjoint attaching subsets with the same handle subsets. Their corner roundings agree outside disjoint seam collars and are compared by the existing corner-rounding isotopies inside them. The normal coordinates are unchanged; hence these are independent **framed** attachments, not merely independent core spheres. For exact parametrization bookkeeping, write $A,B$ for the two framed attachments in the common lower surface. Let $d_A$ and $d_B$ be the identifications to the respective first intermediate surfaces, and let $e_{B|A}$ and $e_{A|B}$ identify the second surgered surfaces with the common upper surface. Denote by $d_A^B$ and $d_B^A$ the maps extended over the other, disjoint handle. The actual identification from the simultaneous two-handle model to the upper level gives $e_{B|A}\circ d_A^B\simeq e_{A|B}\circ d_B^A$ under the canonical identification of the two simultaneous quotient surfaces. To verify this equality, on the complement of the two attaching regions both maps are the same normalized flow from the lower to the upper level. On either handle part they are obtained from the same local model coordinates followed by the same outgoing regular flow. Their collar adjustments differ only by the supported corner-rounding isotopies just described. This proves the displayed isotopy and supplies the outgoing-map rule at the crossing. It is precisely the extra condition missing from an unparametrized “critical heights interchange” statement.

**What finite event reduction now establishes.** Choose parameter values immediately before and after each of the finitely many events, and divide the remainder into finitely many regular intervals. Retain a regular level between each pair of critical values on each regular slice. Steps 2.1 and 3.1 compare the induced elementary handle bands along regular intervals by relative diffeomorphism, framed attaching isotopy, changes of handle-coordinate frame, and insertion/removal of empty product bands. Step 4.1 compares the two sides of each crossing by interchange of two independent framed attachments, with its displayed outgoing-map rule. The cubic normalization in [F1] and step 1.1 compare the two sides of each birth by a geometrically cancelling adjacent-index pair, carrying all later attaching data and the final boundary map by the actual supported cancellation comparison. In particular, this proves finite reduction of the **Morse-induced elementary handle descriptions** along the constructed path. Empty ends, disconnected manifolds, and index $0/n$ births are included: the formulas allow $\operatorname{ind}Q=0$ or $n-1$, and no connected-level or nonempty-end assumption occurred. The supplied Morse/handle correspondence realizes any specified finite handle description by such Morse data. To use the reduction as a move theorem for presentations where the cancellation boundary identification has been suppressed, one must still prove that the chosen suppression preserves the actual end parametrization; the explicit move above instead retains that identification throughout. It is not a proof that arbitrary relative surgery diagrams are related by ordinary Kirby moves.

Fix a complex modular ribbon fusion category as in [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]], with finite simple-label set $I$, tensor unit $\mathbf1$, and dual label $i^*$ for each $i$. Define the **handle object**

$$H=\bigoplus_{i\in I}i\otimes i^*.$$

For an oriented marked surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g$ with ordered marked points labeled by objects $W_1,\ldots,W_n$, fix a parametrization and the standard handle decomposition used to read its labels. The associated algebraic state space is

$$V(\Sigma;W_1,\ldots,W_n)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}\!\left(\mathbf1,\, W_1\otimes\cdots\otimes W_n\otimes H^{\otimes g}\right).$$

The empty tensor product is $\mathbf1$ and $H^{\otimes0}=\mathbf1$. Reversing the orientation of a marked boundary circle replaces its label $W$ by the left dual $W^*$. This formula defines a vector space only; mapping-class operators, bordism maps, independence of parametrization, and gluing are not asserted here.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit $\mathbf 1$ and a finite set $I$ of isomorphism classes of simple objects. Fix a braiding $c$ and a ribbon twist $\theta$. The induced pivotal map is $j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, where $u$ is the Drinfeld morphism of [[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Throughout this pair we use the associated spherical pivotal structure: $j$ is part of the data, and sphericality means $\dim_j(X)=\dim_j(X^\vee)$ for every object, as in [[def-spherical-structure]]. Its trace is $\operatorname{tr}_j(f)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_Xf)$ for $f\in\operatorname{End}(X)$.

Write $0$ for the unit label and $i^*$ for the dual of $i$. Put $N_{ij}^k=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}(k,i\otimes j)$, $d_i=\operatorname{tr}_j(1_i)$, and $s_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}_j(c_{j,i}c_{i,j})$. Define $D^2=\sum_{i\in I}d_i^2$. The unnormalized Hopf-link matrix is $s=(s_{ij})$. The ribbon fusion category is **modular** when $s$ is invertible. When $D^2\ne0$, either square root $D$ defines the normalized matrix $S=s/D$; for a modular category, [[lem-modular-hopf-matrix-squared]] proves this nonvanishing. No positivity of the general $d_i$ or of $D$ is assumed.

An object of a monoidal category is **rigid** if it has both a left dual and a
right dual in the sense of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]].

A monoidal category is **rigid** if every object in it is rigid.

Muger's notes also use the word **autonomous** for the same condition, and
Joyal-Street use **compact** in the non-symmetric setting.

Let $(-)^{\vee\vee}$ be the monoidal endofunctor of
[[thm-the-double-dual-is-a-monoidal-functor]].

A **pivotal structure** on a rigid monoidal category is an isomorphism of
monoidal functors

$$a:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{\sim}(-)^{\vee\vee}.$$

Equivalently, it is a natural family of isomorphisms
$a_X:X\xrightarrow{\sim}X^{\vee\vee}$ such that

$$a_{X\otimes Y}=a_X\otimes a_Y,\qquad a_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$$

after transporting along the monoidal structure of the double-dual functor.

A **multifusion category** is a finite semisimple multitensor category. A
**fusion category** is a finite semisimple tensor category. In particular the
unit of a fusion category is simple, whereas a multifusion unit may split.

Let $u$ and $v$ be parenthesised tensor words on the same ordered letters
$x_1,\dots,x_n$. Then there exists a unique canonical natural isomorphism
$E_u\Rightarrow E_v$. Equivalently, any two canonical morphisms from $u$ to $v$
are equal.

Let $\mathcal C$ be modular with $S=s/D$ as in [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. For simple labels $i,j,k$,

$$N_{ij}^k=\sum_{x\in I}\frac{S_{ix}S_{jx}S_{k^*x}}{S_{0x}}.$$

For simultaneous diagonalization, define the fusion matrix $N_i$ with rows indexed by the second input $j$, columns indexed by the output $k$, and entries $(N_i)_{j,k}=N_{ij}^k$. Then

$$N_iS=S\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{S_{ix}}{S_{0x}}\right)_{x\in I}.$$

This is the algebraic formula; no complex conjugation is used.

Let $\mathcal C$ be modular under [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. Let $C$ be the charge-conjugation matrix, $C_{ij}=\delta_{i,j^*}$. Then

$$s^2=D^2C.$$

In particular $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2\ne0$, so either square root $D$ gives an invertible normalized matrix $S=s/D$ with $S^2=C$.

Let $\mathcal C$ be the spherical ribbon fusion category of [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. For simple labels $i,j$,

$$s_{ij}=(\theta_i\theta_j)^{-1}\sum_k N_{ij}^k\theta_kd_k,$$

and, for simple labels $x,i,j$,

$$s_{xi}s_{xj}=d_x\sum_kN_{ij}^ks_{xk}.$$

Also $s_{ij}=s_{ji}$, $s_{i^*j^*}=s_{ij}$, $s_{i0}=d_i$, and $d_{i^*}=d_i$. Consequently $h_x(i)=s_{xi}/d_x$ extends linearly to a unital ring character of the fusion ring.

derivations.claim: Choose the right-duality maps on $i^*$ induced by the pivotal structure. Concretely, from the left maps $b_i,e_i$ and pivotal $j_i$, take $b_i^R=(1_{i^*}\otimes j_i^{-1})b_{i^*}$ and $r_i=e_{i^*}(j_i\otimes1_{i^*})$. The left snakes for $i^*$, with naturality and tensor compatibility of $j$, give $(r_i\otimes1_i)(1_i\otimes b_i^R)=1_i$ and $(1_{i^*}\otimes r_i)(b_i^R\otimes1_{i^*})=1_{i^*}$. These also follow directly from the right-dual data in [F2]. Fix all parentheses through [F4]. Finite semisimplicity gives $p_{i\alpha}g_{j\beta}=\delta_{ij}\delta_{\alpha\beta}1_{i^*}$ and $\sum g_{i\alpha}p_{i\alpha}=1_X$. The maps $G,F$ are therefore typed finite sums between the specified Hom spaces.

Substitute the displayed $F$ into $G$. Interchange separates the middle composite into the right snake $(1_{i^*}\otimes r_i)(b_i^R\otimes1_{i^*})=1_{i^*}$. Thus $GF(z)=\sum_{i,\alpha}(g_{i\alpha}p_{i\alpha}\otimes1_Y)z=z$. No dimension scalar appears because the projections are composition-dual, not trace-dual.

Conversely, for $f:\mathbf1\to X\otimes i$ put $g_f=(1_X\otimes r_i)(f\otimes1_{i^*}):i^*\to X$. The other right snake gives $f=(g_f\otimes1_i)b_i^R$. In $F(G_i(f\otimes k))$, the $j\beta$ term contains $p_{j\beta}g_f:i^*\to j^*$, which is zero for $j\ne i$ and a scalar $\gamma_\beta$ for $j=i$. The same snake gives its second factor as $\gamma_\beta k$. The sum of the first factors multiplied by those scalars is $(\sum_\beta g_{i\beta}p_{i\beta}g_f\otimes1_i)b_i^R=f$. Hence $FG_i(f\otimes k)=f\otimes k$. Decomposable tensors span each finite tensor product, so $FG=1$ on the entire direct sum, including zero Hom blocks. A basis change $g'=gA$, $p'=A^{-1}p$ cancels in the finite sum for $F$, proving independence of all auxiliary summand bases.

For a nonseparating cut, [F1] and direct-sum additivity identify the target with the stated Hom space into $X\otimes H$. Its inclusions and projections satisfy $\sum_i u_iv_i=1_H$ and $v_iu_j=\delta_{ij}1_{i\otimes i^*}$. Thus $GF=1$ and the $(i,j)$ block of $FG$ is $\delta_{ij}1$, exactly as in the Statement. All multiplicity coordinates remain inside their Hom spaces; none is removed by these simple-label sums.

Naturality on every uncut factor follows by composing the written evaluation, inclusion and projection words and using bifunctoriality; the inverse is natural because it is the inverse of that same map. For two disjoint cut pairs, expand their two finite resolutions before any contraction. Evaluations or inclusions on distinct leg pairs commute by interchange. For separating cuts, insert the actual identities $\sum gp=1$ at their two seams; both orders give the same product of coupon inclusions and projections, regrouped as finite sums. If one summand is produced by the first cut, applying its resolution of identity gives the same all-cuts coupon word. Associators comparing the two fixed tensor words agree by [F4]. Adjacent swaps therefore identify every ordering of finitely many disjoint cuts. Composing the reverse cutting maps cancels each adjacent $F/G$ pair by steps 2.1–3.1. This proves iterated algebraic sewing and its full inverse, with empty sums and empty cut lists included.

The three-marked sphere has dimension $N_{i_1i_2}^{i_3^*}$; by [F5] this equals $\sum_x S_{i_1x}S_{i_2x}S_{i_3x}/S_{0x}$. The zero-, one- and two-marked spheres follow from the corresponding entries of $S^2=C$: their dimensions are $1$, $\delta_{i0}$ and $\delta_{i,j^*}$. Sewing pants and handles using the proved inverse maps gives all finite products with $H^{\otimes g}$. At a separating seam the simple-label sum is $\sum_a S_{ax}S_{a^*y}=\delta_{xy}$, by symmetry, dual-label symmetry and $S^2=C$. At a nonseparating seam its same-index value is $1$. Combining the powers of $S_{0x}$ gives exactly $2-2g-n$. Induction over the finite seam list proves the displayed dimension formula for every $g,n\ge0$. In particular the unmarked torus dimension is $|I|$. This proves an algebraic identity from actual Hom decompositions and Verlinde; it makes no unproved assertion about surgery independence.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Every morphism of the
framed oriented tangle category $\mathcal T$ of
[[def-the-framed-oriented-tangle-category]] is a finite composite of tensor
products of identities, crossings, cups, caps and full twists.

A complete presentation on this elementary family is Turaev's reduced
presentation (3.1.a), (3.2.a)--(3.2.h), **together with** the expressions
(2.5.d)--(2.5.e) and (3.1.b)--(3.1.c) defining its additional orientation
variants. Thus two elementary words represent the same framed tangle exactly
when these relations and the strict monoidal axioms relate them.

Here the source's $X^\delta$ denotes our $X^\delta_{+,+}$, its
$Z^\delta$ denotes our $X^{-\delta}_{+,-}$, and its $Y^\delta$ denotes our
$X^{-\delta}_{-,+}$; its $T^\delta$ denotes our $X^\delta_{-,-}$.
The source's positive cup and cap are $\cup_+$ and $\cap_+$, and its
$\varphi,\varphi'$ are $\varphi_+^+,\varphi_+^-$.
The reduced generators are therefore $X^\delta_{+,+}$,
$X^{-\delta}_{+,-}$, $\varphi_+^{\pm1}$, $\cup_+$ and $\cap_+$.
The other cups, caps and crossings are the expressions above; a twist on a
negative strand is obtained by bending the corresponding twisted positive
strand with a cup and cap. Turaev's convention that a positive strand points
downwards is transported to ours by reversing all strand orientations; this
preserves composition, tensor product and framed isotopy. Crossing
superscripts in his mixed-orientation pictures are oriented signs, explaining
the minus signs in the dictionary.

The reduced relations are Yang--Baxter, the two zig-zags, inverse crossings
and twists, curl slide, the bent-crossing inverse relation (3.2.g), and the
twist-square relation (3.2.h). For example, the latter has the well-typed form

$$(\varphi_+^+)^2=(\cap_+\otimes1_+)(1_-\otimes X^+_{+,+})(X^-_{+,-}\otimes1_+)(\cup_+\otimes1_+).$$

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) with
chosen left duals ([[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]), braiding $c$
([[def-braiding]]) and twist $\theta$, and let $X\in\mathcal C$. Write
$X_{+1}:=X$ and $X_{-1}:=X^{\vee}$. In a strict model of $\mathcal C$
([[thm-every-braided-monoidal-category-is-monoidally-equivalent-to-a-strict-braided-one]])
there is a unique strict monoidal functor

$$F_X\colon\mathcal T\longrightarrow\mathcal C$$

from the framed oriented tangle category $\mathcal T$ with

$$F_X(+)=X,\qquad F_X(-)=X^{\vee},$$

$$F_X\bigl(X^{+}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=c_{X_\varepsilon,X_{\varepsilon'}},\qquad F_X\bigl(X^{-}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=(c_{X_{\varepsilon'},X_\varepsilon})^{-1},\qquad F_X(\cup_{+1})=\operatorname{coev}_X,\qquad F_X(\cap_{+1})=\operatorname{ev}_X,\qquad F_X(\varphi^{\pm1}_{+1})=\theta_X^{\pm1},$$

where the cup and cap are the coevaluation and evaluation maps attached to the
chosen left duals and the signs are the blackboard conventions of
[[def-the-framed-oriented-tangle-category]]. The remaining elementary tangles
of $\mathcal T$, those carrying a negative sign at a cup, cap or twist, receive
the values forced by these data through the relations. Explicitly put
$j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, with $u$ as in
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Then

$$F_X(\cup_-)=(1_{X^\vee}\otimes j_X^{-1})\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee},\qquad F_X(\cap_-)=\operatorname{ev}_{X^\vee}(j_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}),\qquad F_X(\varphi_-^{\pm1})=\theta_{X^\vee}^{\pm1}.$$

These are the right coevaluation and evaluation on $X$ induced by the ribbon
structure; they need no identification $X^{\vee\vee}=X$ on objects. For a general ribbon
category the same assignment determines a strong monoidal functor, unique up to
the canonical coherence isomorphisms of the strictification. Isotopic framed
tangles are equal morphisms of $\mathcal T$, so $F_X$ is an invariant of framed
tangles. Uniqueness needs no choice.

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category ([[def-monoidal-category]]).

A **braiding** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural isomorphism

$$c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\longrightarrow Y\otimes X$$

natural in both variables ([[def-natural-isomorphism]]) such that, for all
objects $X,Y,Z$,

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(1_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z),$$

and

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1}=(c_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1}\circ(1_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

These are the two **hexagon identities**. The invertibility of each
$c_{X,Y}$ is part of the data, not a consequence of the hexagons.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided rigid monoidal category with braiding $c$, and
fix left duals $X^\vee$ for all objects together with the dual-morphism
operation of [[def-the-dual-of-a-morphism]].

A **twist** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural automorphism
$\theta\in\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C})$ such that

$$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$$

for all objects $X,Y$ and $\theta_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$.

A **ribbon structure** is a twist satisfying the dual-compatibility condition

$$(\theta_X)^\vee=\theta_{X^\vee}.$$

An object of a monoidal category is **rigid** if it has both a left dual and a
right dual in the sense of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]].

A monoidal category is **rigid** if every object in it is rigid.

Muger's notes also use the word **autonomous** for the same condition, and
Joyal-Street use **compact** in the non-symmetric setting.

In a braided rigid monoidal category there is a natural isomorphism

$$u_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee},$$

called the **Drinfeld morphism** (or **Drinfeld isomorphism**), defined by

$$X\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X\otimes X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{c_{X,X^\vee}\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^\vee\otimes X\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Write

$$d_{X,Y}:X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\sim}(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$$

for the monoidal comparison of the double-dual functor. Then

$$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}.$$

Thus $u$ need not be monoidal: the double braiding is precisely its
monoidality obstruction.

Let $(\mathcal C,c)$ be a braided monoidal category. Then there exists a strict
monoidal category $\mathcal D$, a braiding $c^{\mathrm{str}}$ on $\mathcal D$,
and a monoidal equivalence $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ such that $F$ is a
braided monoidal functor.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Work first in [F4]'s strict model. Write $b_Y:\mathbf1\to Y\otimes Y^*$, $e_Y:Y^*\otimes Y\to\mathbf1$, $r_Y=e_{Y^*}(j_Y\otimes1)$ and $b_Y^R=(1\otimes j_Y^{-1})b_{Y^*}$. Assign the listed generator values and each coupon its morphism. Slice any generic diagram between all crossings, extrema, recorded twists and coupon levels, then evaluate by categorical tensor product/composition. The strand-only equations of [F1] hold with arbitrary branch colors: Yang–Baxter follows by the naturality/hexagon expansion on $U,V,W$; each inverse and snake has its own actual color; the bent-crossing equation is the arbitrary-$V,W$ composite in [F2]; its inverse-order proof and opposite braiding give all signs; and the twist-square computation of [F2] applies to each arbitrary single $Y$. Redundant orientation variants are its right-dual composites applied separately to each color. Thus no equality of unequal objects or single-color specialization is used to justify multicolored relations.

For $f:|A|\to|B|$, the two displayed crossing/coupon equations are exactly naturality of $c$; multiplying by its inverses gives both underpass versions. Expanding each tensor-list crossing by the two hexagons writes the actual finite word of crossings of one band with all inputs/outputs of the coupon. Upward bands are their dual tensor objects and use the already checked bent-crossing formulas, so these equations cover every orientation. For full rotations define $\Theta_\varnothing=1$ and $\Theta_{A\otimes Y}=c_{Y,A}c_{A,Y}(\Theta_A\otimes\theta_Y)$. Balancing inductively gives $\Theta_A=\theta_{|A|}$, including all individual twists and all pairwise full-bunch crossings. Naturality gives $\theta_{|B|}f\theta_{|A|}^{-1}=f$, exactly the input-bunch inverse/output-bunch full rotation, with no deleted framing twist.

For $f:A\otimes Y\to B$ define its typed left mate $f^\flat=(f\otimes1_{Y^*})(1_A\otimes b_Y):A\to B\otimes Y^*$. The inverse is $(1_B\otimes e_Y)(f^\flat\otimes1_Y)$. Substitution and the two snakes show both composites are identities on these Hom spaces. The other bends use $b_Y^R,r_Y$ and their two snakes. Iteration supplies every signed-list orientation and the needed double-dual comparison $j$; two full dualizations are consistent because $j_Bf=f^{**}j_A$. Coupon composition/tensor rules are the actual equalities $gf$ and $f\otimes g$. Thus all evaluations of bent or subdivided coupons have explicitly inverse composites, with no unnamed duality scalar.

To prove that these equations suffice geometrically, take a boundary-relative graph isotopy and choose disjoint solid rectangular neighborhoods of its finitely many coupons, carried along their tracks. Compactness and finite time subdivision permit smaller such moving neighborhoods disjoint from all other bands except their incident fixed collars. Any homotopy of their frame motions is realized by an ambient isotopy there: prescribe its velocity on each rectangle, multiply by a smooth cutoff in its disjoint moving neighborhood and integrate the resulting time-dependent vector field. Its flow fixes the external collars and carries the incident band collars. Time subdivision keeps these supports disjoint. This reduces frame control to finitely many paths in $SO(3)$ with fixed endpoint frames.

Every resulting rotation loop can be homotoped relative endpoints to planar rotations. Explicitly, unit quaternions form $S^3$ and $q:v\mapsto qvq^{-1}$ gives a locally invertible two-sheeted map onto $SO(3)$ with kernel $\{\pm1\}$. A smooth loop in $S^3$ misses a point after a small perturbation and contracts by stereographic projection to $\mathbb R^3$, so $S^3$ is simply connected. Hence an $SO(3)$ loop is classified by whether its lift ends at $+1$ or$-1$. A planar $2\pi$ rotation lifts from $+1$ to$-1$, so planar rotations realize both classes. The cutoff extension of step 2.3 realizes the homotopies on the graph. It follows that the isotopy reduces to motions keeping coupons parallel to the projection plane with horizontal based edges, together with finitely many planar $\pm2\pi$ coupon rotations. The latter are the complete twist relation of step 2.1.

For the remaining motions protect smaller coupon rectangles and keep their incident band collars fixed. Apply [F1]'s generic movie construction to the exterior core arcs, with its perturbation cutoffs vanishing in those collars. Away from coupons its event list is unchanged. At a protected rectangle there are also generic isolated edge tangencies and corner passages; they are retained, not excluded by a false codimension count. In a small disk a smooth-edge tangency has the form $y=u^2+s$ against the edge $y=0$, possibly with both signs reversed. The spatial strand is strictly above or strictly below the coupon in that disk, since the actual graph is embedded; compactness gives a fixed nonzero height separation there. Attachments lie strictly inside the coupon bases, so the disk may be chosen disjoint from every attachment collar. A corner passage is a strand crossing the two-edge junction transversely; its local resolution is given below. Multiple simultaneous events and higher-order edge contacts add a condition to these already retained normal forms, and only those higher degeneracies are excluded by independent jets.

Resolve an edge tangency as follows. Shrink the coupon a little inside its protected neighborhood, replacing each moved attachment by a short parallel identity strip; this changes neither its color nor its input/output tensor order. The same spatial height separation keeps the external strand disjoint throughout. The small U-shaped strand segment $y=u^2+s$ now gives two successive entries/exits past the shrunken edge. Separate them in slicing height and bend its turn by the explicit mate bijection of step 2.2. Each straight passage is a naturality equation from step 2.1 or its inverse. When only part of the short based strips lies in that small disk, enlarge the local word by inserting the missing crossings paired immediately with their inverses outside the coupon. In algebraic terms the full naturality word is $C_B(f\otimes1)=(1\otimes f)C_A$, where $C_A=c_{|A|,Z}$ and $C_B=c_{|B|,Z}$, or its other-side/inverse version. The completed event is this exact equation pre/post-composed with the same exterior words $L,R$; expand $C_A,C_B$ by the hexagon to match the actual based-strip order. Removing the adjacent inserted inverse pairs recovers the two original readings of the event. No cancellation is moved through $f$, and no naturality for a partial input subobject of $f$ is asserted: the missing input and output crossing words can differ. For the two consecutive passages of the U segment, complete both together, so their exterior words on each fixed side are inverse. Those words reduce to $C_A^{-1}C_A=1$ on the input side and $C_BC_B^{-1}=1$ on the output side, with their respective actual tensor types. Retract the auxiliary bend by its snake. Thus the entire edge-tangency event changes no evaluated morphism. The negative quadratic contact reverses this derivation. A cap instead of a cup uses the inverse mate, an upward strand uses $Z^*$, and an underpass uses the inverse-crossing naturality, all explicitly established in step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2. This covers both orientations, over/under choices, both edge sides and both contact signs. The local shrink only alters attachment-free portions of the protected rectangle, so a base-edge event is treated exactly like a side-edge event; short based strips are included in the sublist completion just described.

For a corner passage choose a disk containing that corner but no attachments. Round or cut off the corner of the protected coupon inside that disk, joining the unchanged two based-edge portions by a smooth arc. This is a planar isotopy of an attachment-free part of the coupon and changes no morphism or tensor list. The external strand stays spatially separated above/below it. Perturb the rounded arc slightly so the corner passage is replaced by two ordinary edge passages and, if the strand turns back in that disk, one quadratic edge tangency. The two possible routes around the old corner differ by the consecutive passage and its inverse; their expanded words cancel as in step 5.1. Thus restoring the corner yields the same value. The four corners differ only in which edge is a base edge; all attachments remain outside the disk, so step 5.1's sublist completion applies to each. This supplies the corner events instead of excluding their generic isolated times.

A coupon level may cross an exterior extremum level or a crossing level at an isolated time; these slicing events are also retained. If their support disks are disjoint from the protected rectangle, their generator words exchange by interchange. If adjacent in projection, shrink the rectangle as in step 5.1 so the extremum/crossing lies outside it. The induced strand passages are the partial/full naturality words already resolved there; a cup or cap adjacent to the coupon is handled by step 2.2's mate bijection and its inverse snake, and a crossing of its short incident strips is moved by [F1]'s cup passage or third move before the naturality word. Moving the coupon back cancels the inserted inverse words. Thus neither a slicing extremum nor a crossing-level event is silently removed from the movie. If two projected coupon rectangles pass each other, shrink one and move its short incident strips past the other successively, then exchange their disjoint levels. The complete identity is $c_{|B|,|D|}(f\otimes g)=(g\otimes f)c_{|A|,|C|}$, obtained by the two naturality equations successively; edge/corner events during this shrink were handled in step 5.1, step 6.1. This covers all valences and the empty tensor list. The retained event list is exhaustive because every remaining regular projected arc/coupon incidence is transverse, every nonregular one has precisely one of the stated edge/corner normal forms after the generic perturbation, and all exterior core singularities and framing events are [F1]'s list.

There are finitely many events by [F1]'s compactness/relative genericity argument applied to this finite graph with its protected rectangle collars. Every event preserves the composite by step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1; between them only slicing levels and disjoint-factor interchange change. The whole framed isotopy therefore preserves evaluation. The generator assignment preserves composition/tensor products and the empty diagram by definition; every diagram has the sliced form, so it also proves uniqueness. Transport through [F4]'s strong monoidal equivalence gives the claimed evaluation in the original category, with all chosen dual comparisons inserted as in [F2]. Only [A1]'s inherited countable choice is used; all additional neighborhoods, frame adjustments and word operations are finite.

Consider finite oriented framed ribbon graphs with boundary collars, bands colored by arbitrary objects of $\mathcal C$, and coupons colored by arbitrary morphisms between the tensor products of their incident signed objects. There is a unique monoidal evaluation assigning each coupon its declared morphism, crossings the braiding or its correctly typed inverse, cups/caps the chosen duality maps and their ribbon-induced opposite variants, and full twists $\theta^{\pm1}$. It is invariant under every boundary-relative framed graph isotopy and preserves composition, tensor product and the empty graph. More precisely, for a signed list $A=(Y_1^{\epsilon_1},\ldots,Y_p^{\epsilon_p})$, put $|A|=\bigotimes_sY_s^{\epsilon_s}$, with $Y^-=Y^*$. For a coupon $f:|A|\to|B|$, its strand passages and full rotation are the complete composites

$$c_{|B|,Z}(f\otimes1_Z)=(1_Z\otimes f)c_{|A|,Z},\qquad c_{Z,|B|}(1_Z\otimes f)=(f\otimes1_Z)c_{Z,|A|},\qquad\theta_{|B|}f\theta_{|A|}^{-1}=f.$$

A **multifusion category** is a finite semisimple multitensor category. A
**fusion category** is a finite semisimple tensor category. In particular the
unit of a fusion category is simple, whereas a multifusion unit may split.
For every simple object $i$ of a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit and pivotal map $j$, its pivotal dimension $d_i=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_i)$ is nonzero.

For $s\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)$ write $\ell_Z(s)$ and $r_Z(s)$ for its left and right actions on $Z$, transported from $s\otimes1_Z$ and $1_Z\otimes s$ by the unit constraints.

1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.
   If $r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))=\ell_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))$, this becomes
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
   In particular multiplicativity holds when every unit scalar has equal left and right actions on every object. This condition holds in a braided category, and also in a $k$-linear monoidal category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$.
4. For every endomorphism $c:X\to X$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$.

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(q\ell_{Y^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_R(p))).$$

It reduces to multiplicativity under the analogous equality of scalar actions, in particular under either sufficient condition above.
