Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category ([[def-monoidal-category]]).

A **braiding** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural isomorphism

$$c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\longrightarrow Y\otimes X$$

natural in both variables ([[def-natural-isomorphism]]) such that, for all
objects $X,Y,Z$,

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(1_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z),$$

and

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1}=(c_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1}\circ(1_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

These are the two **hexagon identities**. The invertibility of each
$c_{X,Y}$ is part of the data, not a consequence of the hexagons.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: For each $X$ choose actual $u_{i,a}:i\to X$, $v^{i,a}:X\to i$ with $v^{i,a}u_{j,b}=\delta_{ij}\delta_{ab}1_i$ and $\sum_{i,a}u_{i,a}v^{i,a}=1_X$. Define $\iota_X=\sum_{i,a}\iota_i(u_{i,a}^*\otimes v^{i,a}):X^*\otimes X\to B$. Changing a multiplicity-space basis multiplies the two entries by inverse matrices, leaving this sum unchanged. For $f:X\to Y$, expand its scalar simple blocks $v_Yfu_X$ in the two decompositions. This gives the exact dinaturality equation $\iota_Y(1_{Y^*}\otimes f)=\iota_X(f^*\otimes1_X)$. If another family $t_X:X^*\otimes X\to Z$ obeys that equation, its finite decomposition is $t_X=\sum_{i,a}t_i(u_{i,a}^*\otimes v^{i,a})$. Thus the unique map $t:B\to Z$ with $t\iota_i=t_i$ satisfies $t\iota_X=t_X$. This proves the coend property explicitly, including uniqueness, without an existence or Fubini theorem.

Define the required structural maps by $\Delta\iota_X=(\iota_X\otimes\iota_X)(1_{X^*}\otimes b_X\otimes1_X)$, $\varepsilon\iota_X=e_X$, and $m(\iota_X\otimes\iota_Y)=\iota_{Y\otimes X}(1_{X^*}\otimes c_{X,Y^*\otimes Y})$. The last target uses $(Y\otimes X)^*=X^*\otimes Y^*$, or its canonical dual comparison. These formulas define maps first on the finitely many simple summands. Dinaturality, braiding naturality and the explicit dual-mate identities in [F1] show that their stated words hold for arbitrary $X,Y$, proving well-definedness under every choice of decomposition. Substituting the first two words gives $(1_B\otimes\varepsilon)\Delta\iota_X=(\iota_X\otimes e_X)(1_{X^*}\otimes b_X\otimes1_X)=\iota_X$ by a snake; the opposite snake gives $(\varepsilon\otimes1_B)\Delta=1_B$ too. No other Hopf algebra axiom is needed.

Fix simple $j,k$ and decompose each $i\otimes j$ using $u_{k,a}:k\to i\otimes j$ and $v^{k,a}:i\otimes j\to k$, with $v^{k,b}u_{k,a}=\delta_{ab}1_k$. Set $F_{i,a}=(v^{k,a}\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes b_j):i\to k\otimes j^*$ and $G_{i,a}=(1_i\otimes r_j)(u_{k,a}\otimes1_{j^*}):k\otimes j^*\to i$. Their inverses as adjunction correspondences insert $e_j$ or $b_j^R$ and retract a snake, so the $F$ and $G$ families span the respective simple multiplicity spaces. Define $\operatorname{ptr}_j(a)=(1_i\otimes r_j)(a\otimes1_{j^*})(1_i\otimes b_j)$ on $a\in\operatorname{End}(i\otimes j)$. The displayed words give $G_{i,b}F_{i,a}=\operatorname{ptr}_j(u_{k,b}v^{k,a})$. Closing in stages and then cyclically gives $\operatorname{tr}_i(G_{i,b}F_{i,a})=\operatorname{tr}_{i\otimes j}(u_{k,b}v^{k,a})=\operatorname{tr}_k(v^{k,a}u_{k,b})=\delta_{ab}d_k$. Since $i$ is simple, $G_{i,b}F_{i,a}=\delta_{ab}(d_k/d_i)1_i$; compositions with different simple labels vanish. Consequently the actual complete trace-dual resolution on $k\otimes j^*$ is $\sum_{i,a}d_iF_{i,a}G_{i,a}=d_k1_{k\otimes j^*}$. This includes every fusion multiplicity and uses no positivity.

For the two-$\Omega$ slide, cut its participating components near the attaching band and place those endpoint pairs adjacently below the remaining graph. Evaluating that exterior with variable cut colors gives $T_{X,Y}:X^*\otimes X\otimes Y^*\otimes Y\otimes U\to V$, retaining arbitrary other boundary factors and coupons. It is dinatural in the two surgery variables: a morphism inserted on their paths passes crossings by [F1]'s naturality, twists by twist naturality and bends by its explicit inverse mate formulas; no coupon lies on a surgery component itself. Define $\Phi:B\otimes B\otimes U\to V$ by its simple restrictions $\Phi(\iota_i\otimes\iota_j\otimes1_U)=T_{i,j}$. step 1.1's finite decomposition proves $T_{X,Y}=\Phi(\iota_X\otimes\iota_Y\otimes1_U)$ for all $X,Y$. This is the full exterior factorization, including arbitrary external coupons, not a claim that those coupons are natural as functions of their own graph colors.

For $a\in\operatorname{End}(k\otimes j^*)$ define the literal composite $T_{kj}(a)=(1_{k^*}\otimes1_k\otimes e_j)(1_{k^*}\otimes a\otimes1_j)(b_k^R\otimes1_{j^*}\otimes1_j):j^*\otimes j\to k^*\otimes k$. It sends the identity to $b_k^Re_j$. Substituting $F,G$ gives $T_{kj}(F_{i,a}G_{i,a})=(u_{k,a}^*\otimes v^{k,a})(1_{j^*}\otimes b_i^R\otimes1_j)$. To check every bend, first expand $F$: its $b_j$ and the final $e_j$ retract by the $j^*$ snake, leaving $v^{k,a}$ on $i\otimes j$. In the other half use $(1_{k^*}\otimes u_{k,a})b_k^R=(u_{k,a}^*\otimes1_{i\otimes j})b_{i\otimes j}^R$, the dual-mate coevaluation identity. Expand $b_{i\otimes j}^R=(1_{j^*}\otimes b_i^R\otimes1_j)b_j^R$; the $r_j$ in $G$ retracts the outer right snake. The remaining word is exactly the stated $u^*,b_i^R,v$ composite, with domain $j^*\otimes j$ and target $k^*\otimes k$. Applying $T$ to step 2.2's resolution thus proves the complete morphism identity $\sum_{i,a}d_i(u_{k,a}^*\otimes v^{k,a})(1_{j^*}\otimes b_i^R\otimes1_j)=d_kb_k^Re_j$.

Put $\Lambda=\sum_i d_i\iota_ib_i^R$. Braiding naturality at $b_i^R$ says $c_{j,i^*\otimes i}(1_j\otimes b_i^R)=b_i^R\otimes1_j$. Hence the multiplication word gives $m(\iota_j\otimes\Lambda)=\sum_i d_i\iota_{i\otimes j}(1_{j^*}\otimes b_i^R\otimes1_j)$. Expand $\iota_{i\otimes j}$ using step 1.1 and apply step 3.1 separately for each output $k$. The result is $\sum_k d_k\iota_kb_k^Re_j=\Lambda e_j$. The $\iota_j$ are all summand inclusions, so this is the full identity $m(1_B\otimes\Lambda)=\Lambda\varepsilon$. step 2.1 consequently gives $\Gamma(1_B\otimes\Lambda)=(1_B\otimes\Lambda\varepsilon)\Delta=1_B\otimes\Lambda$, and precomposing with $\Lambda$ gives $\Gamma(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda)=\Lambda\otimes\Lambda$. This is a full-channel calculation and does not use a simple-meridian projector, modular inversion, Gauss sums or surgery normalization.

Inserting $\Lambda$ at a component cut is exactly the finite formal coloring $\Omega$: $b_i^R$ closes its two oriented cut endpoints and its coefficient is $d_i$. Reversing that component's orientation replaces $i$ by $i^*$; dual-mate compatibility of $j$, ribbon twist duality, and sphericality $d_i=d_{i^*}$ give the same evaluated graph after reindexing the sum. Thus no independent antipode or integral theorem is needed for orientation reversal. Moving a pair of $\Lambda$ cuts past each other also does not change their value, since naturality gives $c_{B,B}(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda)=\Lambda\otimes\Lambda$ from $c_{\mathbf1,\mathbf1}=1$.

The complete endpoint word created by the framed band sum on those two cuts is $(\iota_X\otimes\iota_{Y\otimes X})(1_{X^*}\otimes1_X\otimes1_{X^*}\otimes c_{X,Y^*\otimes Y})(1_{X^*}\otimes b_X\otimes1_X\otimes1_{Y^*}\otimes1_Y)$, exactly $\Gamma(\iota_X\otimes\iota_Y)$. To read it geometrically, follow the rectangle of the attaching band: the slid strand turns around one end, making $b_X$ and its $X^*$ return; its new parallel follows the stationary strand in its specified framing; at the other end $X$ passes the ordered pair $Y^*,Y$, giving $c_{X,Y^*\otimes Y}$ with its hexagon expansion. The two parallels have cable color $Y\otimes X$ and reversed dual cable $X^*\otimes Y^*$. The new parallel follows the entire stationary component outside the little band ball: applying the same exterior $\Phi$ to $\iota_{Y\otimes X}$ accounts for that whole cable. Every exterior crossing cables by the hexagons and every exterior twist by balancing. Thus no false assertion that the global band sum is supported in the attaching-band ball is made. Its full evaluation is $\Phi(\Gamma(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda)\otimes1_U)$, equal to $\Phi(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda\otimes1_U)$ by step 4.1. The rectangle's framing is retained: any twist in it or in the stationary parallel is read on both sides by the same cable twist word, never discarded by an unframed move.

For an open strand keep its fixed color $Y$ and its entire factor $Y^*\otimes Y$, rather than imposing coend dinaturality in a coupon-dependent graph variable. The displayed operator $\widehat\Gamma_Y$ first sends $Y^*\otimes Y$ to $(Y^*\otimes Y)\otimes(Y^*\otimes Y)$ by $1_{Y^*}\otimes b_Y\otimes1_Y$, then sends only the second pair through $\iota_Y$ before multiplication with the surgery variable. step 4.1 implies $m(\iota_Y\otimes\Lambda)=\Lambda e_Y$, by step 1.1's finite decomposition if $Y$ is not simple. Substitution into this exact lifted word gives $\widehat\Gamma_Y(1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes\Lambda)=(1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes\Lambda e_Y)(1_{Y^*}\otimes b_Y\otimes1_Y)=1_{Y^*\otimes Y}\otimes\Lambda$ by the left snake. For simple $j$ the same identity also follows by applying the actual projection $B\to j^*\otimes j$ to $\Gamma(\iota_j\otimes\Lambda)=\iota_j\otimes\Lambda$. Hence it is an identity on the complete open-color factor, not only after a categorical trace.

Fix the actual colored graph and its coupons, and cut only a short interior segment of the strand to be slid. After bending that segment the exterior has type $(Y^*\otimes Y)\otimes B\otimes U\to V$. Its factorization through $B$ uses dinaturality only along the $\Omega$ surgery component, exactly as in step 2.3; the first object $Y$ and every graph coupon remain fixed. The band reading of step 5.2 now uses $\widehat\Gamma_Y$ on that fixed first factor, so step 5.3 equates its before/after composites with the entire fixed exterior. To make the finite-cut method fully explicit, write $1_Y=\sum_{j,a}u_{j,a}v^{j,a}$ and insert that resolution on the short segment before bending. On each term absorb the actual $u_{j,a},v^{j,a}$ into its two adjacent exterior graph portions. Its local segment is now the fixed simple $j$ and step 5.3 applies to that term with those very coupons held constant. Summing restores exactly the original graph; basis independence is the matrix identity $\sum u v=1_Y$. No family of arbitrary coupons indexed by variable $X$ is moved through a universal dinaturality argument.

The bending used in step 6.1 is injective on the relevant open-graph Hom space: for $f:A\otimes Y\to C$, its mate is $(f\otimes1_{Y^*})(1_A\otimes b_Y)$, with inverse $(1_C\otimes e_Y)(-\otimes1_Y)$; their composites are the two snakes. Other incident orientations use $b_Y^R,r_Y$ with their inverse mates. Thus equality of the bent expressions proves equality of the original open-strand morphisms before any closure. If the segment is part of a more complicated coupon-bearing graph, all portions outside its short cut, including junction coupons, are precisely the fixed exterior of step 6.1, so the same equality proves their slide as well. Opposite slide directions read the equality backwards; other orientations and either ordering of the two participating components use step 5.1's explicit dual reindexing and cut interchange. This covers all framed colored-strand and $\Omega$-component cases in the Statement.

All calculations are identities of finite categorical composites, and hence survive arbitrary exterior pre/post-composition and tensor factors. No $D$, Gauss sum, normalized surgery invariant or topological presentation theorem was used. In a surgery application a band slide preserves the component count and changes the linking matrix by $B\mapsto P^tBP$, with $P$ the integral elementary basis change adding the stationary attaching vector to the slid one, so signature is preserved even when singular; that observation adds no assumption to the ribbon identity just proved. citations.quote: For every simple object $i$ of a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit and pivotal map $j$, its pivotal dimension $d_i=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_i)$ is nonzero.

Let $\mathcal C$ be modular under [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. Let $C$ be the charge-conjugation matrix, $C_{ij}=\delta_{i,j^*}$. Then

$$s^2=D^2C.$$

In particular $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2\ne0$, so either square root $D$ gives an invertible normalized matrix $S=s/D$ with $S^2=C$.

Let $\mathcal C$ be the spherical ribbon fusion category of [[def-modular-ribbon-category-and-hopf-link-data]]. For simple labels $i,j$,

$$s_{ij}=(\theta_i\theta_j)^{-1}\sum_k N_{ij}^k\theta_kd_k,$$

and, for simple labels $x,i,j$,

$$s_{xi}s_{xj}=d_x\sum_kN_{ij}^ks_{xk}.$$

Also $s_{ij}=s_{ji}$, $s_{i^*j^*}=s_{ij}$, $s_{i0}=d_i$, and $d_{i^*}=d_i$. Consequently $h_x(i)=s_{xi}/d_x$ extends linearly to a unital ring character of the fusion ring.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit $\mathbf 1$ and a finite set $I$ of isomorphism classes of simple objects. Fix a braiding $c$ and a ribbon twist $\theta$. The induced pivotal map is $j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, where $u$ is the Drinfeld morphism of [[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Throughout this pair we use the associated spherical pivotal structure: $j$ is part of the data, and sphericality means $\dim_j(X)=\dim_j(X^\vee)$ for every object, as in [[def-spherical-structure]]. Its trace is $\operatorname{tr}_j(f)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_Xf)$ for $f\in\operatorname{End}(X)$.

Write $0$ for the unit label and $i^*$ for the dual of $i$. Put $N_{ij}^k=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}(k,i\otimes j)$, $d_i=\operatorname{tr}_j(1_i)$, and $s_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}_j(c_{j,i}c_{i,j})$. Define $D^2=\sum_{i\in I}d_i^2$. The unnormalized Hopf-link matrix is $s=(s_{ij})$. The ribbon fusion category is **modular** when $s$ is invertible. When $D^2\ne0$, either square root $D$ defines the normalized matrix $S=s/D$; for a modular category, [[lem-modular-hopf-matrix-squared]] proves this nonvanishing. No positivity of the general $d_i$ or of $D$ is assumed.

An object of a monoidal category is **rigid** if it has both a left dual and a
right dual in the sense of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]].

A monoidal category is **rigid** if every object in it is rigid.

Muger's notes also use the word **autonomous** for the same condition, and
Joyal-Street use **compact** in the non-symmetric setting.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a rigid monoidal category, let $a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ and $b:Y\to Y^{\vee\vee}$, and suppress the monoidal and chosen-dual comparison maps. For $s\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)$ write $\ell_Z(s)$ and $r_Z(s)$ for its left and right actions on $Z$, transported from $s\otimes1_Z$ and $1_Z\otimes s$ by the unit constraints.

1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.
   If $r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))=\ell_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))$, this becomes
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
   In particular multiplicativity holds when every unit scalar has equal left and right actions on every object. This condition holds in a braided category, and also in a $k$-linear monoidal category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$.
4. For every endomorphism $c:X\to X$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$.

The corresponding right-trace duality, additivity and cyclicity statements hold. For right-trace inputs $p:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$ and $q:Y^{\vee\vee}\to Y$, the general tensor formula is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(q\ell_{Y^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_R(p))).$$

It reduces to multiplicativity under the analogous equality of scalar actions, in particular under either sufficient condition above.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals. Consider finite oriented framed ribbon graphs with boundary collars, bands colored by arbitrary objects of $\mathcal C$, and coupons colored by arbitrary morphisms between the tensor products of their incident signed objects. There is a unique monoidal evaluation assigning each coupon its declared morphism, crossings the braiding or its correctly typed inverse, cups/caps the chosen duality maps and their ribbon-induced opposite variants, and full twists $\theta^{\pm1}$. It is invariant under every boundary-relative framed graph isotopy and preserves composition, tensor product and the empty graph. In a strict model it is strict monoidal; transport gives the corresponding strong monoidal evaluation in $\mathcal C$.

More precisely, for a signed list $A=(Y_1^{\epsilon_1},\ldots,Y_p^{\epsilon_p})$, put $|A|=\bigotimes_sY_s^{\epsilon_s}$, with $Y^-=Y^*$. For a coupon $f:|A|\to|B|$, its strand passages and full rotation are the complete composites

$$c_{|B|,Z}(f\otimes1_Z)=(1_Z\otimes f)c_{|A|,Z},\qquad c_{Z,|B|}(1_Z\otimes f)=(f\otimes1_Z)c_{Z,|A|},\qquad\theta_{|B|}f\theta_{|A|}^{-1}=f.$$

Their tensor-list expansions, all inverse-crossing versions and the explicit dual-mate formulas supply every coupon move; the claim includes zero-input/output coupons and all band orientations. No assumption that all colors are tensor powers of one object is imposed.

Let $\mathcal C$ be modular with $p_\pm=\sum_i\theta_i^{\pm1}d_i^2$, $D^2=\sum_i d_i^2$, and $\kappa=p_+/D$. Then

$$p_+p_-=D^2,\qquad \kappa^{-1}=p_-/D.$$

$$\tau(M_L)=D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F(L_\Omega)$$

is invariant under adding/removing a disjoint $\pm1$-framed $\Omega$ unknot; it gives $\tau(S^3)=D^{-1}$ and $\tau(S^2\times S^1)=1$. The same normalized graph evaluation is invariant under full framed surgery-component handle slides and colored-strand slides over surgery components, with all arbitrary exterior graph coupons retained. A topological theorem asserting completeness of these and relative moves is a separate supplier.

derivations.claim: Choose actual finite simple inclusions $u_{k,a}:k\to X$ and projections $v^{k,a}:X\to k$ from a direct sum, with $v^{k,a}u_{l,b}=\delta_{kl}\delta_{ab}1_k$ and $\sum_{k,a}u_{k,a}v^{k,a}=1_X$. Inserting these two identities on either side of any coupon $f:X\to Y$ gives its complete expansion $f=\sum_{k,a,b}u^Y_{k,b}(v_Y^{k,b}fu^X_{k,a})v_X^{k,a}$. Off-diagonal simple terms vanish by Schur's lemma; every remaining middle term is a scalar. Thus this expansion is independent of basis and respects composition/tensor products. Since $\operatorname{tr}_k(v^{k,a}u_{k,b})=d_k\delta_{ab}$, trace-dual projections are $v^{k,a}/d_k$, and the trace-dual resolution is $1_X=\sum_{k,a}d_k u_{k,a}(v^{k,a}/d_k)$. Reversing an edge applies the dual functor and reverses the composite, preserving the identity.

Trace multiplicativity and Frobenius reciprocity give $d_id_j=\sum_kN_{ij}^kd_k$ and $\sum_i d_iN_{ij}^k=d_kd_j$. Summing the balancing expression $s_{ij}=(\theta_i\theta_j)^{-1}\sum_kN_{ij}^k\theta_kd_k$ therefore gives $\sum_i\theta_i d_i s_{ij}=p_+\theta_j^{-1}d_j$. Multiply by $s_{j^*,k}$ and sum over $j$. The identity $\sum_js_{ij}s_{j^*,k}=D^2\delta_{ik}$ gives $p_+\sum_j\theta_j^{-1}d_js_{j^*,k}=D^2\theta_kd_k$. At $k=0$, reindexing $j$ by $j^*$ yields $p_+p_-=D^2$. Consequently $p_\pm\ne0$ and $\kappa^{-1}=p_-/D$.

For the unit label, put $x_a=u_{0,a}$, $y_a=v^{0,a}$. Then $y_ax_b=\delta_{ab}$ and $P_X=\sum_a x_ay_a$ is the unit-isotypic projector. It is the identity on $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X)$ and on the opposite dual pairing, because all nonunit components of a map from or to the simple unit vanish. The bending map $f:k\to X\mapsto(f\otimes1)b_k$ has inverse $z\mapsto(1_X\otimes e_k)(z\otimes1_k)$ by the two snakes. Closing a bent pair $f,g$ gives $\operatorname{tr}_k(gf)$, so the same $d_k$ factors of step 1.1 apply after bending.

The displayed partial trace satisfies $\operatorname{ptr}_Z((f\otimes1)a(g\otimes1))=f\operatorname{ptr}_Z(a)g$ by interchange. Naturality of both braidings consequently makes each $K_+(X)$ natural in $X$. On simple $j$, step 1.2 gives $K_+(j)=p_+\theta_j^{-1}1_j$. Inserting the full direct-sum resolution gives $K_+(X)=\sum_{j,a}u_{j,a}K_+(j)v^{j,a}=p_+\theta_X^{-1}$ for every object. For the negative version, balancing gives $M_{j,i}^{-1}=(\theta_j\otimes\theta_i)\theta_{j\otimes i}^{-1}$, hence $\operatorname{tr}_jK_-(j)=\sum_{i,k}d_i\theta_i^{-1}\theta_j\theta_iN_{ji}^k\theta_k^{-1}d_k=\theta_jd_jp_-$. Divide by $d_j$ and use the same naturality/resolution to obtain $K_-(X)=p_-\theta_X$.

For arbitrary coupons $a:A\to X$ and $b:X\to B$, step 2.2 says $b\theta_X^{\pm1}K_\pm(X)a=p_\pm ba$. Take $X$ to be the tensor product of every oriented strand through the local surgery annulus, using duals for reversed strands. Repeated hexagons expand $M_{X,i}$ into the full encircling strand word; repeated balancing expands $\theta_X$ into all individual twists and pairwise crossings in its full bunch twist. This explicitly identifies the complete signed twist-surgery composite even if exterior coupons join different members of the bunch. If its eliminated framing is $\epsilon=\pm1$ and linking vector is $\ell$, its matrix $B=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}\epsilon&\ell^t\\\ell&A\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ is congruent to $[\epsilon]\oplus(A-\epsilon\ell\ell^t)$ by replacing each remaining vector $z$ with $z-\epsilon\ell_z u$. Thus $m$ decreases by1 and signature by$\epsilon$. Its graph scalar is $p_\epsilon$, and $D^{-1}\kappa^{-\epsilon}p_\epsilon=1$, proving the normalized signed-move equality with its exact framing/signature factors.

The same naturality makes $E_X$ natural. On simple $j$ its scalar is $d_j^{-1}\sum_i d_i s_{ji}=D^2\delta_{j0}$ by $s^2=D^2C$. Inserting step 1.1 proves $E_X=D^2P_X$ on every object, not just a simple strand. Thus $D^{-2}yE_Xx=yx$ for any $x:\mathbf1\to X$, $y:X\to\mathbf1$, with arbitrary coupon networks defining $x,y$.

Rigidity gives $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,i^*\otimes j)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i,j)$, zero unless $i=j$. When $i=j$ its generator is $b_i^R$, and $e_ib_i^R=d_i$ by sphericality. Hence $P_{i^*\otimes j}=\delta_{ij}b_i^Re_i/d_i$. Insert this into $R_{ij}(E_{i^*\otimes j})$. The right snake $(r_i\otimes1_i)(1_i\otimes b_i^R)=1_i$ retracts its first pair, and the left snake $(e_i\otimes1_{i^*})(1_{i^*}\otimes b_i)=1_{i^*}$ retracts the remaining pair. The resulting full morphism is $\delta_{ij}(D^2/d_i)1_{i\otimes i^*}$. derivations.claim: Represent a standard cap by a ball containing one coupon and its marked strands, with one attached solid cylinder for each handle; the two bases of its handle arc are adjacent on the coupon. Reverse the coupon for the opposite raw cap. For a cylinder take two such disjoint standard handlebody neighborhoods in $S^3$ and, for each handle, a zero-framed surgery annulus surrounding its two opposed handle arcs. Choose mutually disjoint products $D_r\times[-1,1]$; inside each, the two handle arcs occupy small cylinders $B_r^-\times[-1,1]$, $B_r^+\times[-1,1]$ in an interior disk $D'_r\subset D_r$. Its surgery annulus is $D_r\setminus\operatorname{Int}D'_r$. Zero-framed surgery replaces its thickening by $D^2\times S^1$, attaching so that each $\partial D'_r\times\{t\}$ bounds a disk. That disk joined to the pair-of-pants $D'_r\setminus\operatorname{Int}(B_r^-\cup B_r^+)$ is an annulus between the two handle boundaries. As $t$ varies these are an annulus product, and the complementary portion of the filling solid torus leaves the ordinary cylinder between the punctured sphere boundaries. The product structures use the same $t$ coordinate on their collars, so they glue to $\Sigma_t\times I$ with its original parametrizations. This is a local coordinate proof of this particular cylinder presentation, not a completeness assertion. Its $g$ surgery annuli are zero-framed and mutually unlinked, so $m=g$, $\sigma(B)=0$.

Reading the oriented two opposed arcs in each disk product gives exactly $R_{ij}(E_{i^*\otimes j})$ of [F1]: the two bends are its specified $b_j,r_i$, and the surrounding annulus is its specified partial-trace meridian. Thus the complete graph word vanishes unless both handle tuples agree, and on $i=j$ it is $D^{2g}/d(i)$ times the identity of $X_{t,i}$. Arbitrary testing coupons give $F_{\rm cyl}(y_j,x_i)=\delta_{ij}D^{2g}d(i)^{-1}y_ix_i$. Multiplying by the actual closed normalization $D^{-g-1}$ gives precisely $Q_t$. Its matrix in composition-dual bases is diagonal, with nonzero entries $D^{g-1}/d(i)$, so its inverse is the stated $N_t$. In particular its geometrically dual testing coupon to a raw basis vector $x_{i,a}$ is $D^{1-g}d(i)y^{i,a}$. This is a computation of the geometric Gram form, rather than confusing $\operatorname{tr}(1_{i\otimes i^*})=d_i^2$ with the cup/cap composition $r_ib_i=d_i$.

The raw pairing is perfect because a finite simple decomposition of $X$ has a unit-isotypic basis $x_a:\mathbf1\to X$, $y_a:X\to\mathbf1$ with $y_ax_b=\delta_{ab}$, and all nonunit summands contribute zero. Thus every capped multilinear functional defines a unique map $A_M$. Multiplying its outgoing block $j$ by $N_{\Sigma_{\rm out}}=D^{\sum_q(1-g_q)}d(j)=D^{\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)$ gives the exact block formula in the Statement. Empty output has correction1. For disconnected bordisms the caps and all normalizations multiply, yielding the exponent $-m-b_0(M)+\chi_{\rm out}/2$. The distinction between raw and geometrically dual cap coordinates is essential: one either inserts $N$ explicitly or absorbs it into the opposite cap basis.

In the cylinder formula the coefficient is $D^{-g-1+(1-g)}d(i)=D^{-2g}d(i)$, and the graph word is $D^{2g}/d(i)$ by step 2.1. Hence $Z_\alpha(\mathrm{cyl})=1$ on every color/multiplicity block. The outgoing empty-graph ball has $m=\sigma=0$ and $\chi_{\rm out}/2=1$, so its vector is1. The incoming ball has empty output and is multiplication by $D^{-1}$. Gluing them gives $D^{-1}=\tau(S^3)$, and the sphere cylinder has raw functional $D^{-1}yx$ corrected by $N_{S^2}=D$. Inserting an arbitrary handlebody coupon $x$ below the cylinder graph gives the decorated handlebody; the same local cancellation sends it to $x$. Thus every vector of the stated Hom space is realized. Tensoring gives the disconnected cylinder law. The empty bordism gives1, and disjoint union tensors the states, caps, $N$ factors and closed graph evaluations, proving its law.

For $r$ connected boundary tensor objects $X_q$ choose unit-channel composition-dual bases $x_{q,a},y_q^a$. Define $\iota(\bigotimes_qx_q)=\bigotimes_qx_q$ from $\bigotimes_q\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X_q)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,\bigotimes_qX_q)$, and define $\pi(z)=\sum_{a_1,\ldots,a_r}(\bigotimes_qx_{q,a_q})[(\bigotimes_qy_q^{a_q})z]$. These maps are independent of the chosen unit bases because their object-level projectors are. For a special graph with disconnected input/output set $F_0=\pi_{\rm out}\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,F)\iota_{\rm in}$ before the finite surgery-color sum. This retains precisely the required tensor-product channels; the larger Hom of the object tensor product is not silently identified with that tensor product of Hom spaces.

First suppose $M_1,M_2$ are connected and the common surface is connected of genus $G$. Stack their special graphs across a separating sphere. Each pair of matching open handle arcs joins to a surgery annulus, adding exactly $G$ components. A neighborhood of the separating sphere and the joined arcs is a sphere product with $2G$ one-handles; the disk/annulus surgery model of step 1.1 turns it into the product of the common genus-$G$ surface with an interval. Its complementary two pieces are the original bordisms with their cap parametrizations unchanged. Thus the stacked graph presents their glued bordism. If the middle color tuple is $j$, its new annulus weight is $d(j)$; categorical composition and the complete unit-channel resolutions therefore give $F_0(\Omega)^l_i=\sum_j d(j)F_0(\Omega_2)^l_jF_0(\Omega_1)^j_i$. This identity includes the sum over a full basis of every multiplicity Hom space, namely $\sum_ax_{j,a}y^{j,a}=P_{X_j}$ acting as the identity on its Hom from the unit.

Write $m_1,m_2$ for the old component counts and $\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma$ for the actual old/stacked matrix signatures. Here $m=m_1+m_2+G$. The product of the two block coefficients of step 3.1 has $D$ exponent $-m_2-1+\chi_{\rm out}/2-m_1-1+(1-G)=-m_1-m_2-G-1+\chi_{\rm out}/2$, exactly that of the composite. Its remaining factors are exactly $d(l)d(j)$ as in step 5.1. The sole discrepancy is therefore $\kappa^{\sigma_1+\sigma_2-\sigma}$, proving the stated formula without assuming a Maslov theorem.

If the middle surface has $r\ge1$ components and total genus $G$, add $r-1$ zero-framed family-meridians at the separating sphere, each surrounding all arcs in one specified middle family. After the $G$ handle-annulus surgeries, the separating cylinder is the connected genus-$G$ surface product. Each family-meridian surgery compresses along its separating circle: remove $S^1\times I\times I$ and attach the two products $D^2\times I$ using the original collars. The $r-1$ disjoint compressions split it into exactly the $r$ prescribed middle surface products, so that graph presents the actual composite. If instead all $r$ family-meridians are added, the last one bounds a disk in one of those products and its surgery adds a separated $S^1\times S^2$ connected-sum factor. This proves the local graph-stacking model, including the previously missing disconnected families; it does not assert that all surgery diagrams of a bordism can be connected by these models.

Use the all-$r$ graph, with $m^+=m_1+m_2+G+r$. step 4.2 says its meridian sum inserts $D^{2r}$ times exactly the necessary $\iota\pi$ between the two exterior maps. Thus $F_0(\Omega^+)^l_i=D^{2r}\sum_jd(j)F_0(\Omega_2)^l_jF_0(\Omega_1)^j_i$. The closed connected-sum rule is $\tau(N\#P)=D\tau(N)\tau(P)$: place the two surgery links in disjoint balls; their component counts and signatures add, while the product normalization has one additional $D^{-1}$. The same argument holds for external cap graphs away from the sum balls. Since $\tau(S^1\times S^2)=1$, the extra factor is $D$ and must be divided out. Assume AC. Let $M$ be a compact $R$-oriented $n$-manifold with boundary $A$, for a commutative unital ring $R$. Cap with its relative fundamental class gives isomorphisms, for every integer $p$,
$$S_p:H^p(M;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M,A;R),\qquad T_p:H^p(M,A;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R).$$
Here both maps send a class $a$ to $a\cap[M,A]$ in the displayed target. Empty boundary recovers Poincaré duality. Disconnected and empty manifolds are included. AC is inherited only from the exhaustion and local universal-coefficient arguments in Poincaré duality.

Let $M$ be a compact $R$-oriented $n$-manifold with boundary $A$, where $R$ is a commutative unital ring and the orientation is supplied on $M\setminus A$. Its **relative fundamental class** is the unique class
$$[M,A]\in H_n(M,A;R)$$
whose restriction at every interior point is the prescribed local generator. Existence and uniqueness, including manifolds with closed components, are proved in [[lem-a-collar-identifies-boundary-local-homology-with-the-pair-fundamental-class]].

The **induced boundary orientation** is the orientation whose local generator at $x\in A$ is the restriction of $\partial[M,A]$, where $\partial$ is the homology pair connector. The same lemma proves that these restrictions are generators and form a continuous section. Thus
$$\partial[M,A]=[A]$$
for this orientation. In tangent-then-inward coordinates its generator is $(-1)^n$ times the tangent generator for the product orientation: this is the outward-normal-first convention. Each component inherits its sign from the supplied interior orientation; there is no further independent selection of signs.

If $A$ is empty, this is the absolute fundamental class and the boundary class is zero. In dimension zero the boundary is empty. Empty $M$ and the zero coefficient ring give the unique zero class. These definitions and their well-definedness use no AC.

For composable chain maps in an abelian category
$$C_\bullet\xrightarrow{f}D_\bullet\xrightarrow{g}E_\bullet,$$
there is an exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(D,C;f)\to H_n(E,C;gf)\to H_n(E,D;g)\to H_{n-1}(D,C;f)\to\cdots.$$

If $Z\subseteq X$ and $\overline Z\subseteq\operatorname{int}_X(A)$, then
inclusion $(X-Z,A-Z)\to(X,A)$ induces isomorphisms
$H_n(X-Z,A-Z;G)\cong H_n(X,A;G)$ for every $n$.

For an open cover $X=U\cup V$, the sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(U\cap V;G)\to H_n(U;G)\oplus H_n(V;G)\to H_n(X;G)\xrightarrow{\delta}H_{n-1}(U\cap V;G)\to\cdots$$
is exact, with middle map $(u,v)\mapsto u+v$.

Assume AC. Let $M$ be a compact oriented smooth 3-manifold as in [[def-oriented-smooth-cobordism]], with closed, possibly disconnected boundary $\Sigma$, and let $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ be inclusion. Extend the direct-sum intersection form of [[def-intersection-form-on-the-homology-of-a-closed-oriented-surface]] to $H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb R)$. The boundary kernel

$$\lambda_M=\ker(i_*:H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb R)\to H_1(M;\mathbb R))$$

is Lagrangian. If $\Sigma$ is empty, this means $\lambda_M=0$ in the zero symplectic space.

Use the Wall-form Maslov convention of [[lem-maslov-index-four-lagrangian-cocycle]]. Let $B\subseteq\overline V\oplus W$ be a finite-dimensional real Lagrangian relation, where the product symplectic form is $-\omega_V\oplus\omega_W$. Write $B(L)=\{w:\exists v\in L,(v,w)\in B\}$ and $B^t(Q)=\{v:\exists w\in Q,(v,w)\in B\}$. For Lagrangians $L,P\subseteq V$ and $Q,R\subseteq W$,

$$\mu_V(L,P,B^t(Q))+\mu_W(B(L),Q,R)=\mu_W(B(P),Q,R)+\mu_V(L,P,B^t(R)).$$

Consequently, for composable Lagrangian relations $A:V_0\to V_1$, $B:V_1\to V_2$, $C:V_2\to V_3$ and specified Lagrangians $\lambda_i\subseteq V_i$, the integer correction $m(B,A)=\mu_{V_1}(A(\lambda_0),\lambda_1,B^t(\lambda_2))$ satisfies

$$m(B,A)+m(C,BA)=m(C,B)+m(CB,A).$$

It vanishes for either identity relation, is additive on direct sums, and for graphs of symplectic isomorphisms $f_1,f_2$ equals $\mu(f_2f_1\lambda_0,f_2\lambda_1,\lambda_2)$. No injectivity, transversality or equal-dimension hypothesis on a general relation is imposed.

Let $(V,\omega)$ be a finite-dimensional real symplectic vector space and let $L_1,L_2,L_3$ be Lagrangian subspaces. Put

$$U_{123}=\frac{L_1\cap(L_2+L_3)}{(L_1\cap L_2)+(L_1\cap L_3)}.$$

For $a\in L_1\cap(L_2+L_3)$ write $a+b+c=0$ with $b\in L_2,c\in L_3$. The form

$$\psi_{123}([a],[a'])=\omega(a,b')$$

is well-defined, symmetric, and nondegenerate. Define $\mu(L_1,L_2,L_3)=\operatorname{sign}(\psi_{123})$. For any four Lagrangians,

$$\mu(L_1,L_2,L_3)+\mu(L_1,L_3,L_4)=\mu(L_1,L_2,L_4)+\mu(L_2,L_3,L_4).$$

Use the category, $D,d_i,\kappa$ and dualities of [[lem-colored-fr-surgery-and-coupon-cancellation]]. For a connected standard genus-$g$ marked surface $t$, put

$$X_{t,i}=W_1^{\epsilon_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes W_n^{\epsilon_n}\otimes\bigotimes_{r=1}^g(i_r\otimes i_r^*),\qquad V_t=\bigoplus_{i\in I^g}\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1,X_{t,i}),\qquad d(i)=\prod_r d_{i_r}.$$

For disjoint surfaces take tensor products and set $V_\varnothing=\mathbb C$. Opposite raw coupon coordinates are $\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_{t,i},\mathbf1)$, with composition pairing. With the standard spine handlebody caps and their reflected opposite caps, the normalized capped-cylinder Gram pairing is

$$Q_t(y_j,x_i)=\delta_{ij}D^{g-1}d(i)^{-1}y_ix_i.$$

Its inverse correction is $N_t|_i=D^{1-g}d(i)1$, extended multiplicatively across surface components. For a fixed special surgery graph $\Omega$ representing a connected parametrized graph bordism $M$, let $m$ and $B$ be its surgery-component count and linking matrix. Define $A_M$ by the raw testing-coupon functional $y(A_Mx)=D^{-m-1}\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}F(\Omega;y,x)$, with finite surgery-color sum understood, and set $Z_\alpha(M)=N_{\Sigma_{\rm out}}A_M$. Then

$$Z_\alpha(M)^j_i=\kappa^{-\sigma(B)}D^{-m-1+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)F_0(\Omega;i,j).$$

Here $\alpha$ denotes the actual reference cap meridians and $F_0$ includes the exact tensor-Hom projections defined below. These fixed-presentation operators satisfy the cylinder, ball, empty and disjoint-union laws. For stacked presentations of composable bordisms,

$$Z_\alpha(M_2M_1)=\kappa^{\sigma(B_1)+\sigma(B_2)-\sigma(B_{\rm comp})}Z_\alpha(M_2)Z_\alpha(M_1).$$

The signatures here are the actual matrices, including the indicated added annuli. No Maslov identification is assumed in this lemma. For disconnected $M$, use the product over its connected components, equivalently the exponent $-m-b_0(M)+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2$. Independence under a complete relative presentation calculus is a separate theorem; this result proves the exact normalization and algebra of its local cap/stacking models. No unweighted anomaly-free functor is asserted.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most

derivations.claim: For any symmetric finite-dimensional real form $q$ on $E$ and subspace $V$, one has $\operatorname{sign}(E)=\operatorname{sign}(q|_V)+\operatorname{sign}(q|_{V^\perp})$, allowing all restrictions to be degenerate. Split off a nondegenerate complement to the radical of $q|_V$, reducing to an isotropic $V$, and discard the ambient radical without changing signatures. For an isotropic basis $v_i$, choose dual vectors $u_j$ with $q(v_i,u_j)=\delta_{ij}$ and replace $u_i$ by $u_i-\frac12\sum_jq(u_i,u_j)v_j$. The resulting pair span has matrix $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&I\\I&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ and signature0. Its orthogonal complement is the nondegenerate reduction of $V^\perp/V$, so its signature is that of $V^\perp$. If $V$ met the discarded ambient radical, first discard those basis vectors. Reintroducing the first nondegenerate orthogonal summand proves the asserted formula.

A surgery trace $W_L$ is $B^4$ with framed two-handles. A handle core capped by a Seifert surface has self-intersection equal to its framing; distinct capped cores intersect by the oriented linking number, counted by pushing their Seifert surfaces normally. Thus its intersection matrix is the actual linking matrix $B_L$, and $\sigma(W_L)=\sigma(B_L)$ even when singular. To identify the stacked trace cut, let the separating sphere bound a three-ball $P\subset B^4$ and take its collar $P\times I_t$. The old $L_1,L_2$ handles lie on their respective side hemispheres. Each new joined-handle surgery circle crosses the equator twice; parametrize its new handle as $h_r=D^2\times D^2\cong I_s\times I_t\times D_z^2$. Only its two opposite attaching patches $\{s=\pm1\}\times I_t\times D_z^2$ meet the middle collar, along two disjoint $D^2\times I_t$ disk products. Its other attaching patches $I_s\times\{t=-1\}\times D_z^2$ and $I_s\times\{t=+1\}\times D_z^2$ lie in the two side hemispheres. The zero framing is exactly the matching of these $z$ coordinates without a rotation; it is available from the explicit paired disk-product presentation in [F4]. Round only the small product corners. This specifies which portions of each original attaching region lie in each piece.

Put $E=H_2(W)$ with its absolute intersection form and $V=\operatorname{im}[H_2(W_1)\oplus H_2(W_2)\to H_2(W)]$. Interior cycles in different pieces are disjoint, and the restriction within each is its original intersection form. Thus the pullback of the form on $V$ is the direct sum of the forms of $W_1,W_2$. Its inclusion kernel is radical because its image intersects every cycle trivially; quotienting by it changes no signature. Hence $\operatorname{sign}(q_W|_V)=\sigma(W_1)+\sigma(W_2)$, and step 1.1 reduces the entire defect to the form on $V^\perp$.

Let $C$ be the union of $P\times I_t$ and those new handles with only their $s=\pm1$ patches attached to that collar. Relative to $C$, each handle is $I_s\times(I_t\times D_z^2)=D^1\times D^3$, attached along $S^0\times D^3$. It is therefore a four-dimensional one-handle relative to the middle collar, although it was a two-handle relative to the original whole attaching circle. All disjoint disk products match, giving the literal product $C=[P\cup(\bigsqcup_r I_s\times D_z^2)]\times I_t=U_G\times I_t$. In particular $H_1(C)=\mathbb R^G$, $H_2(C)=0$, $\sigma(C)=0$. The two side intersections are exactly $(P\times\{\pm1\})\cup(\bigsqcup_r I_s\times\{\pm1\}\times D_z^2)\cong U_G$. The complementary side pieces are the original four-ball halves with their old $L_i$ handles: rounding the product indentations changes only boundary collars; no whole new handle remains on either side. Thus the actual decomposition is $W_{L_{\rm comp}}=W_{L_1}\cup_{U_G}(U_G\times I)\cup_{U_G}W_{L_2}$ with these exact faces. This avoids the false ordinary-handle claim: $B^4$ with $G$ whole attaching-circle two-handles instead has $H_2$ of rank$G$ and is not this middle product.

Use smooth singular chains subordinate to product collars, or a finite smooth subdivision respecting all faces. Excision gives $H_2(W,M_0)=H_2(W_1,M_0)\oplus H_2(W_2,M_0)$. For $z\in H_2(W)$ let $z_i$ be its relative image. Its intersection with any $y\in H_2(W_i)$ is the evaluation of the image of $z_i$ in $H_2(W_i,\partial W_i)$ on $y$: all transverse intersections are in the interior of $W_i$, so enlarging the allowed relative boundary from $M_0$ to $\partial W_i$ does not alter them. Perfection in [F1] therefore gives $z\in V^\perp$ exactly when both those relative images vanish. The triple sequence and excision contain $H_2(M_i,\Sigma)\to H_2(W_i,M_0)\to H_2(W_i,\partial W_i)$. Hence for such a $z$ choose $s_i\in H_2(M_i,\Sigma)$ mapping to $z_i$, and write $a_i=\partial s_i\in K_i$. The boundary of $z$ in the sequence of $(W,M_0)$ is zero, so $a_1+a_2$ maps to zero in $H_1(M_0)$. Thus $a_0=-a_1-a_2\in K_0$ also bounds a relative chain in $M_0$.

Conversely take a triple $(a_1,a_0,a_2)\in K_1\oplus K_0\oplus K_2$ with sum0. Choose actual smooth singular one-cycle representatives for $a_1,a_2$, define $a_0=-a_1-a_2$ at the chain level, and choose bounding two-chains $S_i\subset M_i$. Their boundaries may be made those exact one-cycles by adding their homology corrections in face collars. Thus their sum is a closed two-cycle with product collars and no unaccounted central two-chain in $\Sigma$. Push its faces slightly into $W$, obtaining $z(a)\in V^\perp$ by step 3.1. Different bounding choices in $M_1,M_2$ change it by boundary classes and hence globally radical classes; choices in $M_0$ change it by classes in $V\cap V^\perp$, radical on $V^\perp$. For an arbitrary original $z$ of step 3.1, the constructed $z(a)$ has the same image in $H_2(W,M_0)$, so $z-z(a)$ is in $\operatorname{im}H_2(M_0)\subset V$ and in $V^\perp$, again radical. The triple construction therefore surjects onto the nondegenerate reduction of $V^\perp$.

Near $\Sigma$ choose $u\ge0$, $v\in\mathbb R$ and $p\in\Sigma$, with $\operatorname{or}(W)=du\wedge dv\wedge\operatorname{or}(\Sigma)$, $W_1=\{v\le0\}$, $W_2=\{v\ge0\}$, $M_0=\{v=0\}$, $M_1=\{u=0,v\le0\}$ and $M_2=\{u=0,v\ge0\}$. The $M_0$ face of $W_1$ has orientation $-du\wedge\operatorname{or}\Sigma$; its outward boundary vector at $u=0$ is $-\partial_u$ and gives precisely $\operatorname{or}\Sigma$. The outer face of $W_1$ is $-dv\wedge\operatorname{or}\Sigma$, so the convention $\partial W_1=M_0-M_1$ gives $\operatorname{or}(M_1)=dv\wedge\operatorname{or}\Sigma$ and its boundary has that same $\Sigma$ orientation. Similarly $\operatorname{or}(M_2)=-dv\wedge\operatorname{or}\Sigma$ and its boundary agrees. These coordinates realize exactly the Statement's signs. A bounding strip along a normal ray coordinate $t$ pointing away from the corner has orientation $-dt\wedge a_i$, giving boundary $a_i$ at $t=0$.

All outside-corner intersections can be removed explicitly. The three faces have disjoint tubular neighborhoods away from a fixed corner collar. For the first and second surfaces supported on the same face choose two distinct constant small normal levels into $W$: distinct positive $u$ levels for $M_1,M_2$, and distinct $v$ levels for the seam $M_0$. Even if their underlying chains in a three-face meet along curves, their normal levels separate them. Different faces remain in disjoint neighborhoods. In the annular transition to the corner normal fan, interpolate the two same-face levels to two ordered endpoints on the boundary of that face's angular sector. Linear interpolation preserves their order; the three sectors are disjoint there. Hence no intersections occur in the transition annulus either. For both triple chains use the exact chain equality $a_1+a_0+a_2=0$ of step 4.1, so no extra central $\Sigma$ surface is hidden in this construction. The perturbations are realized on the finitely many smooth chain pieces with product collars; bilinear intersection counts add over these pieces, so the argument applies even when a representing singular chain has multiple components or self-intersections.

Move the second triple's junction in the normal half-plane to $(\epsilon,\epsilon)$, leaving its negative-$v$ ray directed from that point toward the negative-$v$ boundary ray, its positive-$v$ ray toward the positive boundary ray, and its seam ray toward increasing $u$. Choose the already ordered transition paths of step 6.1. In the central disk the only crossing is then between the first seam ray and the second negative-$v$ ray. The first tangent is $+\partial_u$ and the second points toward decreasing $v$, so their determinant in the ordered normal plane $(\partial_u,\partial_v)$ is negative. The two oriented surface tangent bases are $(-t_0,a_0,-t_1',a_1')$. Moving the first surface's $\Sigma$ tangent past the second surface's normal tangent gives one minus; the two displayed prefixed minus signs cancel. Thus the four-dimensional sign is minus the normal crossing sign times the $\Sigma$ crossing sign, yielding $q_W(z(a),z(a'))=\omega(a_0,a_1')=-\omega(a_1,a_0')$. The last equality is symmetry of the Walker form for order $(K_1,K_0,K_2)$, using isotropy and the sum-zero equations. step 6.1 excluded every other intersection. Therefore the pullback remaining form is $-\psi_W$. The surjection of step 4.1 carries radicals to radicals, and its kernel is radical because the target pairing pulls back to this form. Its nondegenerate reduction is consequently isometric to that of $V^\perp$. Combining this with step 1.1, step 2.1 proves $\sigma(W)=\sigma(W_1)+\sigma(W_2)-\mu_W(K_1,K_0,K_2)$. Disconnected faces give orthogonal sums throughout.

Absorb $U_G\times I$ into the first trace by a boundary collar extension, preserving its other cap faces and signature. Apply step 7.1 to its remaining gluing face with the second trace. For $r>1$ middle components, first cut $P$ along the $r-1$ disjoint separating disk products of [F4]'s family-meridian model. They separate precisely the specified arc families; their thickened compressions split the middle product into the disjoint products $U_{g_q}\times I_q$, with all other side pieces unchanged. The redundant final family-meridian in the alternative all-$r$ graph is a separated zero-framed trace handle with matrix$[0]$ and signature0; omit it for the actual cut. Thus the same argument applies componentwise, and the incidence-component connected-sum reduction in [F4] adds only zero-signature trace blocks.

The corner surface orientation in step 5.1 is opposite the canonical middle object orientation: it is induced from the incoming face of $M_2$, and $\partial M_2$ contains the negative of that object. The corner kernels identified with its canonical $H_1$ are $K_1=R_1(\alpha_0)$, $K_0=\alpha_1$, $K_2=R_2^t(\alpha_2)$. Indeed Mayer–Vietoris after capping the incoming boundary of $M_1$ says that a middle class dies exactly when it is homologous in $M_1$ to an element of the cap kernel $\alpha_0$; this is precisely $R_1\alpha_0$. The identical outgoing-cap argument gives $K_2$, and the common actual handlebody has kernel $\alpha_1$ by its definition. These use the individual bordisms, not inclusion maps into their final composite. Negating the surface orientation negates the entire Walker form. step 7.1 with the actual trace cut of step 1.2, step 2.2, step 8.1 therefore gives $\Delta\sigma=+\mu_W(R_1\alpha_0,\alpha_1,R_2^t\alpha_2)=\mu_\alpha$. Substituting into [F4] gives $Z_\alpha(M_2M_1)=\kappa^{-\mu_\alpha}Z_\alpha(M_2)Z_\alpha(M_1)$.

This sign can also be checked directly against Turaev's printed convention: his form on $a=a_1+a_2\in L_3$ is $h(a,b)=\omega(a_2,b)=\omega(a_2,a_1')=-\omega(a_1',a_2)=-\psi_W(a',a)$. Symmetry gives $\mu_T=-\mu_W$. His surgery parameter is $\Delta=p_-$, so $D/\Delta=\kappa$ and his anomaly $\kappa^{\mu_T}$ is exactly $\kappa^{-\mu_W}$. This is a sign comparison only; the local Wall proof above does not cite that source theorem as its proof. In particular preserving the prescribed composition $n_{\rm comp}=n_1+n_2+\mu_W$ requires weight action $\kappa^{+n}$, since $\kappa^{-n}$ would duplicate instead of cancel the computed anomaly.

No arbitrary real $\lambda$ needs realization by a geometric handlebody. Keep the actual reference cap meridians $\alpha$ and set $w(R)=\mu_W(\lambda_0,\alpha_0,R^t\alpha_1)+\mu_W(R\lambda_0,\alpha_1,\lambda_1)$, $a(R)=-w(R)$. These spaces are Lagrangian by [F3], even for noninjective relations. To compute its coboundary use [F3]'s proved associative category of weighted relations. The diagonal weight-zero relation $J:(H,\lambda)\to(H,\alpha)$ has the weight-zero diagonal inverse: their composition corrections are $\mu(\lambda,\alpha,\lambda)=0$. For a relation $R$ between the reference objects with weight0, the arrow $J_{\rm out}^{-1}\circ R\circ J_{\rm in}$ between the $\lambda$ objects has exactly weight $w(R)$, by the two displayed middle-space corrections. For composable $A,B$, cancelling adjacent $J$ arrows calculates its weight as $\mu_\alpha+w(BA)$; composing the two $\lambda$ arrows calculates it as $w(B)+w(A)+\mu_\lambda$. Associativity equates these actual weights. Therefore $a(BA)-a(B)-a(A)=\mu_\alpha-\mu_\lambda$, without defining an integer by the desired equality.

Define $Z(M,n;\lambda)=\kappa^{n+a(R_M)}Z_\alpha(M)$. The exponent in its composite is $n_2+n_1+\mu_\lambda+a(BA)-\mu_\alpha=n_2+a(B)+n_1+a(A)$ by step 10.2, so step 9.1 proves strict weighted composition. The correction vanishes when $\lambda=\alpha$, and for the identity relation it is $-\mu(\lambda,\alpha,\alpha)-\mu(\lambda,\alpha,\lambda)=0$. The cylinder and tensor/empty laws of [F4] therefore persist; direct sums add both Maslov terms and $a$. A weight increase by1 acts by $\kappa$ with no anomaly-free assumption. Equivalently the connected block formula is $\kappa^{n+a(R_M)-\sigma(B)}D^{-m-1+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)F_0(\Omega;i,j)$, with [F4]'s multiplicative disconnected version. This proves all stated signature, cap-reference and weight assertions while leaving genuine relative presentation/move completeness to its own theorem. Full AC is inherited precisely through [F1], and countable choice through [F4]; the new form reductions and bases are finite.
